description: Past conflicts have shown that repelling invaders is not our only concern. The valleys of our cantons are devastated with each battle; careful steps must be taken to bring prosperity back to our land.

name: Alpine Defense
description: The $SWI_ADJ$ landscape is dominated by rough terrain, mountains, and valleys. We must find a way to overcome the challenges our environment presents, and to find a way to use it as a weapon against any potential invaders.

name: Haven for Refugees
description: While others exile religious minorities and disruptive figures, we will gladly offer them a home. In $SWI$, they will be able to establish a new life for themselves, and as a result will be inclined to praise our rule.

name: $SWI_ADJ$ Tolerance
description:
Why must we kill each other over obscure issues of transubstantiation and predestination, when we could spend that energy turning our mountain home into a realm united once more?

For that reason, every Canton of $SWI$ will have the ultimate jurisdiction over religious matters in their region. While this will not eliminate all religious strife in our country, it will at least ensure that no matter what someone believes, our people will be able to find a place where they are not persecuted.

name: Masters of Clockwork
description: Some fools think that clockwork is for timekeeping alone, but when one witnesses the power of rotating gears, it is obvious that clockwork can do just about anything one wants it to do. Maybe the Creator of the Universe Himself wound up existence like a clock and let the gears spin on their own, ticking away the centuries. Be that as it may, $SWI_ADJ$ clockmakers are the greatest masters of the art — barring God Himself, of course.

name: $SWI_ADJ$ Enlightenment
description: We do not need to construct a unique identity for our country, since our people readily rally around the banners of their cantons and the ideals of our confederacy. But by funding our most enlightened scholars of our time, we will be able to shape a new age for the $SWI_ADJ$ people, and solidify the unique traits of our #italic Eidgenossenschaft#!. This Helvetism forms the foundation of our Enlightenment.

name: $SWI_ADJ$ Banking
description: We are a sanctuary, not only for persecuted people from other countries, but also for their wealth. In large vaults, hidden away behind strong walls and protected by our most trustworthy soldiers, we will be the best place for every citizen of the poor, war-torn countries of the world to stash their valuables.

name: $paik_system$
description: $paik_system_desc$

name: Sāmanta Feudalism
description: Sāmanta — #italic neighbor#! — is a term denoting vassals and tributary chiefs alike. It is a feudal system that has for centuries acted as one of the pillars of our society. While this arrangement is currently losing prominence, it remains a foundation of our political structure.

name: Kalaripayattu
description: Kalaripayattu — the #italic Practice in the Arts of the Battlefield#! — is an old Indian martial art with its origins in the $malabar_area$. Warriors of our state shall be trained in the arts of Kalaripayattu to ensure their hand-to-hand and melee prowess.

name: $a_paik_infantry$
description: $a_paik_desc$

name: Advanced Paiks
description: $a_late_paik_infantry_desc$

name: Furor Celtica
description: For millennia, our ferocious and agile guerilla warfare has harried our foes, besting them with a devastating succession of evasive skirmishing and blood-curdling charges.

name: Cattle Booleying
description: In $IRE$, cattle-rearing is our way of life. The noble bovine is not only a source of food, but a symbol of wealth. By #italic booleying#!, a system of moving our herds from one distant pasture to another, we can grow that wealth.

name: Insular Monasticism
description: Although we are now aligned with Roman $catholic_ADJ$ practices in principle, religious life in our islands still puts a great focus on lay clergy.

name: Traveling Bards
description: Traditional poets trained in courtly ways crisscross our lands looking for some likely lord to hire them.

name: Guards of the Shannon
description: The fortress of Athlone, standing astride the mighty river Shannon, is the key to controlling the heart of $IRE$. The O'Kellys of $HYM$, long-standing lords of these lands, have fought fiercely to defend their holdings against $norman$ incursions.

name: Hiberno-Norman Keeps
description: Our $norman$ forebears built splendid towers to maintain their grip on the hostile interior of $IRE$.

name: $IRE_ADJ$ Frontier Settlements
description: The land we have seized from the $IRE_ADJ$ is ripe for exploitation. We just need to ensure that only the right sort of people migrate here to settle these cheap crofts.

name: Old Viking Towns
description: The ancient trading ports founded by the Ostmen are still bustling hives of mercantile activity where the canny can get rich.

name: Pale Works
description: Our boundary is defined by light defensive works of dykes and palisades designed to deter our unruly neighbors from launching their irritating raids.

name: Grand Jury System
description: County grand juries levy the cess for roads, bridges, and courthouses. With judges riding the assizes, oversight tightens in every county.

name: $IRE_ADJ$ Establishment
description: A permanent army in $IRE$ — and controlled #italic from#! Ireland — keeps garrisons ready and costs down. For our regular soldiery, this means regular pay. For our logisticians and quartermasters, it means a growing network of barracks that keeps the costs in hand.

name: $IRE_ADJ$ Volunteers
description: Citizen corps are raised for home defense and coastal watch. Drilling at their own expense, they rouse public spirit and stiffen the line.

name: The Hills Speak Celtic
description: Centuries of living under the shadow of conquest have taught our warriors the art of patience and resilience. We can rush headlong into danger, but we can also endure, defend, and strike only when the moment is right.

name: The Western Shore
description: For millennia we have fished, traded, and fought along the wild Atlantic coasts. From these harsh waters, we have learned seamanship unmatched by any rival.

name: The West's Awake
description: After long centuries of silence, the ancient spirit of the Celtic peoples stirs once more, ready to reclaim its place amongst the great civilizations of the world.

name: Celtic Nations
description: Our union is founded on the ideal of uniting the diverse peoples of the Celtic world under a shared banner. Through cooperation, we aim to preserve our heritage, promote our values, and ensure that the Celtic nations thrive together in the face of external pressures and changing times.

name: Celtic Diaspora
description: From crofter to chieftain, many have left our shores through hardship or hope, weaving a far-flung web of kinship that carries our language, customs, and pride to distant lands.

name: Pan-Celticism
description: Our vision of a united Celtic world is more than an ideal - it is a rallying call to all who share our heritage. Together, we forge bonds that reach beyond borders, making our identity as enduring as the hills and seas we call home.

name: Bushidō
description: Although never formally codified into specific rules, the way a warrior should behave is clear: A warrior's duty is to fight and win in battle, and to expand the glory of one's own clan, regardless of the methods needed to achieve that.

name: Land of the Rising Sun
description: $japan_region$ has a long and glorious history. Our unique cultural traditions, our brave soldiers, and our unconquerable geography make us stronger than many other states in our region. The time has come for the Land of the Rising Sun to take its place among the great nations of this world!

name: Ancestral Legacy
description: The ancestral lineage of our clan is well-known, and our reputation is a pillar of our identity — one that we strive at all costs to uphold, as our history both defines us and ensures our right to rule.

name: Shinobi no Mono
description: Information is key to gaining the advantage in any situation. To that effect, we have long since used spies and infiltrators to gather reconnaissance. These $jap_shinobi$ are usually from the samurai class, although they can also be recruited from the local peasant population, and are sent into enemy territory, where they blend in and establish networks of informants.

name: Head-Hunting
description: The achievements of a warrior in battle are only truly noteworthy if they can be proven. To that end, samurai will collect the decapitated heads of enemies they have slain to present them later to their general. The more numerous and more important the heads that a samurai takes, the better the rewards he will receive.

name: Ichiban Yari
description: Drawing first blood in battle is an honor and a good omen, and thus our warriors are eager to land the first strike whenever they have the opportunity to do so.

name: Ashigaru
description: Warfare has always been the domain of the mighty samurai. Recent developments, however, have proved the need for more substantial reinforcements, and thus our battlefields now also include peasant troops. These #italic ashigaru#! will not be just common rabble, however, as their rigorous training and ample battle experience makes them formidable fighters, on equal footing with the samurai.

name: Daiku Construction
description: Traditional carpentry techniques, or #italic daiku#! have been used in $japan_region$ since the earliest days of our history. Our wooden buildings are resilient yet flexible, and admired by many for their beauty and skillful construction. From the lowliest hut to the most elaborate palace, wood is our most universal building resource.

name: Wandering Rōnin
description: It is fairly common for samurai to wander the country in search of the best employment opportunities, switching their allegiance to whoever pays them the most. These warriors come and go like the errant waves, but we can always make use of them.

name: Reformed Land Holding
description: Traditionally, we assessed land value based on size, but this failed to take into account that not all land is the same. From now on, it will be valued according to how much $rice$ can be grown there. This will streamline related economic actions and make it easier to get the best outcomes from our agricultural ventures.

name: Jōkamachi
description: Turbulent times are gravely dangerous for our people, so for safety, they tend to settle around the security of fortified places. These huddles eventually turn into cities, which of course provide commercial and cultural assets in addition to physical protection for those who huddle behind the walls.

name: Terakoya
description: These private schools provide basic education to commoners, promoting literacy, numeracy, and moral values. #italic Terakoya#! play a vital role in fostering a more educated and socially aware populace, contributing to national stability and progress.

name: Codified Bushidō
description: The expected behavior of a warrior is becoming increasingly idealized, with values such as honor and loyalty being given more importance than their actual utility in real battle. This romanticized and codified version of #italic Bushidō#!, however, will improve how our armies are perceived, even if it is not how they actually behave.

name: Mounted People
description: Our people have thrived on horseback for centuries, and these majestic creatures are an integral part of our culture and power. We take immense pride in our unrivalled skills in our equine husbandry and talent for mounted archery, both of which contribute to our supremacy on the battlefield.

name: Falconry Mastery
description: Deeply rooted in our culture, falconry represents a bond forged between our people and these magnificent birds of prey, and we have finely honed our skill in this ancient art. Our falconers are renowned for their ability to train these majestic raptors to hunt and capture prey.

name: Rich Lands
description: Our lands are rich with fertile soil and abundant resources from the prairies to the dense forests, ready to be transformed by our hardy men and women. We will use every tool at our disposal to wisely manage the land we have been gifted, and thereby bring prosperity to every household.

name: Jurchen Honor
description: Our people are enthusiastic about feats of strength and other demonstrations of skill, as each Jurchen feels that by showing off their abilities they earn the respect of their peers. This well-earned self-respect makes our warriors immensely brave, ready to fight anyone.

name: Unite the Tribes
description: Since the birth of our nation, the Jurchen people have been unified and divided into multiple tribes and alliances, and not always friendly ones. This dynamic has been constant for as long as we can remember — as has the urge to unify all our tribes under a single banner. The time has come to satisfy this long-cherished desire!

name: A Leader under the Sky
description: Our people have been divided for too long, and we need someone strong enough to unite them and make the world tremble at our feet. The Sky will direct the acts and thoughts of this leader, and guide us to a bright future.

name: Foraging our Way
description: We are hunters and live in communion with nature, even those of us dwelling in cities. It is in our blood to find the correct path in a dark forest; to know which of Nature's gifts to take with us. This wisdom lets us survive everywhere without difficulty.

name: The Eight Banners
description: The Eight Banner System is the core of our society and military. Through hereditary membership and grants of land and income, the Banners are granted elite status, and for good reason — from the conquest of our neighbors to future campaigns, our dominance depends on their might.

name: Deliberative Council of Princes and Ministers
description: Originally called the 'Council of Deliberation', this body evolved from informal institutions that promoted collaborative governance among the leaders of the realm. The Council's structure has been transformed, focusing on collective aristocratic governance and policy deliberations, mainly in foreign and military affairs. Membership is restricted to military leaders from outside the imperial clan, ensuring elite participation while maintaining the ultimate authority of the ruler.

name: Manchu Script
description: The Manchu alphabet has emerged, combining Classical $mongolian_language$ characters with Jurchen phonetics. This unique writing system facilitates left-to-right vertical column writing. With diverse letter forms and contextual adaptability for initial, medial, final, and isolated positions, it preserves the most subtle nuances of our language.

name: A New Dawn
description: Our nation has been reborn. The old ways of living are gone, like dreams melting into the morning light. It is time for us to face the world as a fully modernized nation.

name: Manchu Reborn
description: As our nation has undergone fundamental transformations, so will our army. The world has opened itself to us, and new challenges will appear on the horizon. If we want to survive in this new paradigm, we have to be ready to act.

name: Arabian Horses
description: The climate of $india$ is suboptimal at best for breeding and raising horses. The horses of $arabia_region$, however, are superb mounts that outclass our local breeds. We will use our trade connections to ensure that we have a steady supply of these horses for our troops.

name: Amir Rebellion
description: Our state was born from the rebellion of Amir Hasan Gangu against the pathetic rule of $DLH$. The victory against the $DLH_ADJ$ Sultanate still lives on in the minds of our own nobility and military to this day.

name: Hindu Elite Integration
description: Although at times a challenge to the sovereignty of the ruler, the noble class is nonetheless useful to our government, as they are crucial in administrating our vast properties. With winning our independence from $DLH$, we gained rulership over almost exclusively $hindu_ADJ$ subjects, while our $muslim_ADJ$ nobles are a small minority, unable to manage the masses. We must expand and stabilize our aristocracy by promoting promising $hindu_ADJ$ candidates into their ranks.

name: Gharbians
description:
Cutting ties with $DLH$ to found our own kingdom has loosened our connection with the $muslim_ADJ$-dominated northern parts of $india$. As our state lacks any form of entrenched $muslim_ADJ$ aristocracy, we are in a precarious situation, and we could end up entirely at the mercy of local $hindu_ADJ$ nobles.
Fortunately, our reputation precedes us. Tales of the riches of the $deccan_region$ are told and retold all over the $muslim_ADJ$ world, and many ambitious fortune-seekers make the sea voyage to our ports. By using the vast riches of $india$ to attract talented westerners, or #italic Gharbians#!, to our court, we can ensure that our country shall never lack able minds to lead our armies, collect our taxes, and rule our subjects.

name: Legacy of Gisu Daraz
description:
$india$ in general, and our state in particular, has a history as a center of Sufi teachings. The efforts of our rulers to attract and patronize Sufi sheiks from all over the world are a testament to the piety and the great spiritual strength of our monarchs and our court.
The state adopting the Sufi concepts of spiritual sovereignty and the inclusive nature of the Sufi teachings themselves will help create an environment where the diverse religious faiths of $bah_gharbians$ and the natives of $deccan_region$ alike can mix and thrive without clashes or unproductive quarrels.

name: Linguistic Melting Pot
description: $deccan_region$ is a region of many languages and cultures; the great influx of people of $iranian_group$, $turkic_group$, $afghan_culture$, and $arabian_group$ descent into these lands has accentuated the cosmopolitan nature of our state. While historically the $persian_language$ language fulfilled the needs of our predecessors, a new mix of local languages — as well as $persian_language$ and $arabic_language$ — has grown increasingly common. This mixture of languages has even become a source of cultural inspiration for emerging artists.

name: Kārimī
description:
For centuries, the Indo-Egyptian trade has been dominated by $egypt_region$-based groups of traders and captains known as the $bah_karimis$. Instrumental in the day-to-day business of $indian_ocean_region$ trade, this merchant organization is now both wealthy and powerful. From the $tamil$ coasts and the ports of the $swahili_culture$ trading cities to the $lower_egyptian_culture$ port cities past the $gulf_aden_province$, sultans, nobles, and commoners alike come to buy exotic goods or borrow money for their projects from the $bah_karimis$.
This organization has lately taken a very active interest in our state, and we only stand to gain from cultivating our relationship with them further.

name: Takht-e-Fīrozā
description: The first thing any guest in our royal audience chamber notices is the Turquoise Throne of our dynasty. This unique piece of royal furniture was originally donated to us by the defeated $telugu$ Raja Kapaya, and it is in many ways the ultimate symbol of our dynasty. Exquisite and splendidly unique, it embodies the riches of the $deccan_region$ and the unusual combination of styles that is the hallmark of our cosmopolitan state.

name: Bahmani Primogeniture
description: Our unusual practice of always passing the throne to the eldest son of the current ruler has at times created some instability in our realm, as power-hungry regents and opportunistic nobles initially showed little hesitation in trying to take advantage of a child ruler or in supporting an envious relative's claim to the throne. By now, however, the practice has become firmly institutionalized, and when the time for succession comes there are very few who would oppose the true heir of our dynasty.

name: Great Madrasa of the $deccan_region$
description: For many years now, our state has drained able men from the greater $muslim_ADJ$ world, while also incorporating the best of the states that came before us. This has created a rich cosmopolitan culture that is not entirely $farsi_culture$, $arabian_group$, $marathi_culture$, $telugu$, nor $kannadiga$ in nature. Creating a major madrasa in our capital would serve to further the development of learning this multitude of cultures and also allow the world to see the greatness of our state.

name: Ligurian Coastal Seafarers
description: Every community along the Ligurian Riviera — from the fishing harbors of Ventimiglia to the hillside villages above La Spezia — has for centuries sent men to sea in small coastal boats, mastering the currents, hazards, and weather of one of the most demanding coastlines in the Mediterranean. This tradition of practical seamanship produced sailors of unusual quality long before any of our cities built deep-water warships, and the coastal cabotage trade that these men sustained carried goods between ports that no inland road could reach as efficiently. This seafaring heritage gives our merchants a natural edge in coastal and regional trade and ensures that any galley fleet we put to sea is crewed by men who already know the water.

name: La Superba
description: We have built our republic on the twin pillars of commerce and credit, pioneering instruments of debt and exchange that have funded our trading posts from the #italic Levant#! to the Black Sea since the early Middle Ages. Our colonies and comptoirs across the Mediterranean are as much diplomatic outposts as commercial ones, granting us a reach that no purely military power could match. This network of finance and statecraft ensures our bankers and envoys work as one, reducing the cost of credit and keeping more ambassadors in our service.

name: Ligurian Merchant Diaspora
description: The merchants of our coast did not wait for the great trading cities to invite them in — they established colonies, agencies, and partnerships in every port they could reach, from the Black Sea settlements of Caffa and Pera to the counting houses of Seville and Lisbon. These #italic Colonie#! operated on networks of trust and kinship that made Ligurian credit as reliable in Alexandria as at home, and the information that flowed along those networks gave our merchants an advantage in every market they entered. This diaspora turns geography from a limitation into an asset, extending our commercial reach far beyond what the size of our fleet alone would justify.

name: Bank of Saint George
description: Founded to consolidate the mounting debts of the republic, the #italic Casa di San Giorgio#! has become one of the most sophisticated financial institutions in Christendom. Private creditors and the state share in its governance, channeling $GEN_ADJ$ wealth into ventures abroad while keeping the cost of borrowing low. This union of public and private capital gives us unmatched capacity to finance our ambitions.

name: Ligurian Spirit of Navigation
description: The Ligurian coast has produced navigators out of all proportion to its size — Cristoforo Colombo, who opened the western Atlantic to Castilian ambition, Giovanni Caboto, who mapped the northern coast of the New World for the English crown, and a generation of pilots whose skills carried them into every ocean that European ships reached. This tradition of producing men willing to sail beyond the horizon with imperfect charts has given Ligurian seamanship a reputation that attracts investment and patronage from courts that would otherwise never look at our small coast. This culture of navigation elevates our standing among foreign powers and draws skilled settlers and fortune-seekers to our harbors from distant lands.

name: The New Republic
description: In the turbulent years of the early sixteenth century, #italic Andrea Doria#! restructured our republic, consolidating the old noble factions into twenty-eight great houses — the #italic Aberghi#! (#italic Alberghi#! in standard Italian: great houses) — and granting us a political stability we had long been denied. That same pragmatic spirit reshaped our fleet, redirecting our naval expertise toward service across the Mediterranean rather than tying us to a single strategic posture. This reinvention allows us to maintain our navy at reduced cost and to convert our war galleys to lighter vessels when the moment demands it.

name: Ligurian Artisan Craft
description: The workshops of the Ligurian coast have developed a tradition of decorative craftsmanship — silver #italic Filigrànn-a#! (#italic Filigrana#! in standard Italian: filigree) from the city's goldsmiths, maiolica fired in the kilns of Albisola, and intricate velvet weaves that our weavers first perfected in the fourteenth century — that found buyers wherever wealthy patrons sought something finer than the common market could supply. This artisan culture thrived in the same workshops that produced the less glamorous goods of daily commerce, giving our craftsmen a flexibility that purely luxury-focused guilds could not match. This tradition of decorative excellence attracts the most skilled artists of the age to settle among us and ensures that the work they produce commands premium prices wherever it is sold.

name: The Age of the $GEN_ADJ$
description: The great banking fairs of #italic Piacenza#! have made $GEN_ADJ$ financiers the indispensable creditors of the Spanish crown and the arbiters of European capital flows for generations. The immense wealth that passes through our hands finds its way into the palaces and villas of our merchant nobility, who have built the most far-reaching commercial network in the Mediterranean world. This supremacy over European finance makes our merchant network more efficient than any rival's, and the trade it channels through $GEN$ fills our treasury with returns drawn from every major commercial circuit in Europe.

name: Reform of the Communal Councils
description: The self-governing communes that had managed Ligurian harbor life for centuries were gradually formalized and rationalized, replacing informal custom with written charters, elected committees, and standardized administrative procedures that reduced the friction of local governance. These reformed councils gave the merchant class a structured forum for managing the affairs of their communities without dependence on noble patronage or distant judicial authority, embedding a civic competence in the institutions of every Ligurian town. This administrative tradition gives our government an unusual depth of trained civic talent and makes our institutions more responsive to the needs of the burghers who sustain our commerce.

name: $GEN_ADJ$ School
description: The prosperity of centuries of trade has made $GEN$ a city of collectors and patrons, and from this milieu there has emerged a distinct #italic $GEN_ADJ$ School#! of painting celebrated for its mastery of dramatic light and rich texture. Artists nurtured in our republic have carried $GEN_ADJ$ taste and prestige to courts and collections across Europe. This flourishing of artistic culture deepens our traditions and extends our influence far beyond what politics alone can achieve.

name: The Ligurian Enlightenment
description: The philosophers and jurists of #italic Liguria#! have engaged as deeply with Enlightenment thought as any school in Europe, arguing that the principles of reason and natural law demand a wholesale rethinking of how states govern and laws are made. We draw on this tradition to reform our institutions from within, replacing custom and privilege with codified procedure and bringing the best administrative minds of the age into public service. This commitment to rational governance makes our laws clearer, our reforms cheaper, and our state harder to destabilize.

name: Porto Franco
description: As the great Atlantic trade routes have drawn commerce away from the Mediterranean, we have answered by declaring our harbor a #italic Porto Franco#! — a free port open to merchants of all nations, exempt from the duties and restrictions that weigh down our rivals. Ships that once bypassed Liguria now put in at our quays, and the city fills again with foreign factors, warehouses, and coin. This openness to all comers turns our harbor into one of the busiest entrepôts of the western Mediterranean, drawing trade and people in equal measure.

name: Municipal Liberties
description: The cities of Lombardy have governed themselves through elected consuls and independent courts since the time of the Lombard League, building a tradition of civic law that no emperor has managed to fully dismantle. We draw on this legacy by codifying these municipal liberties into a formal charter, granting our towns a recognized degree of self-governance in exchange for their loyal contribution of taxes and troops. This compact between the crown and the city keeps our urban population engaged and invested, reducing the friction that bleeds other states dry whenever they need to call on their subjects.

name: Il Biscione
description: The coiled serpent of the Visconti has become the most recognized symbol of power in Northern Italy, stamped on our coins, our seals, and the gates of every city that answers to us. By making the #italic Biscione#! the official mark of the ducal state, we tie the region's loyalty to our dynasty rather than to any one noble faction. This visual authority makes it far harder for rivals to question our rule, and our ambassadors find that the serpent on their credentials opens doors that other Italian lords cannot.

name: The $lombard$ Bankers
description: $lombard$ merchants and bankers have established themselves across European cities for generations, lending to courts and trading houses that find no more reliable source of credit anywhere else. By formalizing this reputation through regulated exchange houses and letters of credit with fixed terms, we make our financial network a deliberate instrument of the state rather than a scattered collection of private ventures. This reach into foreign treasuries gives us a voice in the courts of Europe that our military strength alone could never secure.

name: The Fabbrica del Duomo
description: The Veneranda #italic Fabbrica del Duomo#! has maintained a permanent workforce of stonecutters, engineers, and master builders in continuous employ for generations, treating the Cathedral not as a project with an end but as an institution that trains craftsmen and refines technique for as long as the work demands. We have extended its remit and its funding, ensuring that the knowledge it preserves flows outward to every construction site in our territory. This institution turns Milan into a school of practical building, and the craftsmen it trains are sought across the whole of northern Italy.

name: The Navigli
description: The canal network that threads through the $lombard$ plain started as a simple irrigation system but has grown into the arteries of our entire regional economy, connecting Milan to the Po and carrying grain, timber, and finished goods at a fraction of the cost of road transport. We have invested in widening and deepening these waterways, building new locks that allow heavier barges to move year-round without depending on seasonal water levels. This network cuts the cost of supplying our cities and moving troops, making Lombardy one of the most efficiently administered territories in Italy.

name: The Milanese Armorers
description: A breastplate made in our workshops commands a price that craftsmen in Cologne or Toledo cannot match, and our armories supply courts and captains from Portugal to Poland. We formalize the armorers' guilds under ducal oversight, setting standards that protect our reputation and keep the technical knowledge — and the profit — within our walls. This monopoly on premium military equipment brings us steady revenue and keeps our own troops better equipped than any enemy who has to import their plate from elsewhere.

name: The Lombard Chiaroscuro
description: Michelangelo Merisi, born in a small town near Bergamo, developed a way of painting light and shadow so direct and brutal that it made the work of every other school look artificial by comparison. His followers spread the #italic Chiaroscuro#! technique from our cities to Rome, Naples, and Madrid, and patrons have started to commission works explicitly in the Lombard manner. This reputation turns our cities into destinations for collectors and scholars, and the artists we train are in demand everywhere they go.

name: The Borromean Reform
description: Carlo Borromeo's administration of $MLO$ became the most closely studied model of institutional reform of the age — rigorous reorganization of local hierarchies, standardized training for officials, and regular inspection visits that reached every village in our territory. We adopt his model wholesale, using every institution at our disposal to extend education and discipline throughout our realm. This reform builds a population that is both more literate and more tightly bound to the institutions of the realm, making civic order far easier to maintain.

name: Masters of Silk
description: The mulberry groves and silk workshops of Lake Como and the $lombard$ plain supply the courts of Europe with the finest silk cloth available, and our weavers have refined the production process to a degree that foreign competitors struggle to replicate. We protect this advantage by regulating the export of raw silk and the techniques of our master weavers, ensuring that the value-added work stays within our borders rather than leaving as cheap raw material. This control over the full production chain turns silk from a local trade into a steady source of revenue that holds its value even when other commodity prices fall.

name: Beccaria's Treatise
description: Our city produced Cesare Beccaria, whose treatise on crimes and punishments has become the most-read legal text in Europe, arguing that laws should deter crime through certainty rather than cruelty. By reforming our criminal code along these lines — replacing torture and arbitrary sentencing with proportional penalties and open courts — we create a legal system that the urban population sees as fair rather than predatory. This makes our cities easier to govern and more appealing to merchants and investors who know their disputes will be resolved by law rather than by bribes.

name: La Manifattura
description: In the foothills around Bergamo and Como, English spinning frames and power looms are replacing the old cottage workshops, and the mills running off Alpine streams have begun producing cloth faster and cheaper than any hand-weaver can match. We have invested in this transition by building company towns and bringing in foreign engineers to train our workers, turning what was a scatter of family looms into a modern industry. This manufacturing base makes Lombardy the productive heart of Italy, and the wealth it generates flows into every corner of our territory.

name: Teatro alla Scala
description: We have raised a theatre on the site of the old church of Santa Maria alla Scala, large enough to seat two thousand and fitted with stage machinery that no other house in Europe can match. The first night drew every ambassador, merchant prince, and noble family who could claim a connection to Milan, and within a season premieres here were being discussed from London to Saint Petersburg. This stage makes our court the cultural arbiter of the continent, and the artists who succeed at La Scala carry our city's name everywhere they travel.

name: Nair Military
description: The Nairs are a diverse group of $hindu_ADJ$ castes from $malabar_area$ and have a long history of involvement with the military. Their experience, as well as their role for the $kalari$, will be of great value in our current conflicts.

name: Tā Moko
description: With the intricate curves and spirals of #italic Tā Moko#!, we ritualistically etch pigment into our very skin, transforming our bodies into living tapestries of honor and history.

name: Ceremonial Haka
description: The ground shakes as our warriors perform the #italic Haka#!, their fierce cries and synchronized movements echoing across the battlefield. This intimidating ceremonial war dance emboldens the heart of every warrior, granting a significant morale boost to land forces.

name: Whakapapa
description: Strength and unity come from knowing one's #italic Whakapapa#!, the intricate web of genealogical connections that binds an #italic iwi#! together. This deep understanding of collective ancestry fosters a united front against all adversities.

name: Te Reo
description: We know that by preserving and nurturing #italic Te Reo#!, our sacred language, we maintain a vibrant connection to our culture and traditions.

name: Rua Kūmara
description: By perfecting the art of growing and storing #italic kūmara#! tubers in specially-constructed #italic rua#!, or storage pits, we can ensure that our bellies are filled even in the harshest of winters.

name: He Whakaputanga
description: The so-called 'Declaration of the Independence of New Zealand' is a document that once and for all establishes a unified $maori_culture$ state that is independent. With the wording fully understood by all sides, our chieftains may finally unite, and be free from foreign interference.

name: Tradition of Military Service
description: $marathi_culture$ cavalrymen have a long tradition of service as 'Bargirs' for the Deccan sultanates. The increased militarization of the Deccan due to the many wars fought in the area has made our cavalry one of the most dangerous forces in $india$.

name: Peasant Soldiers
description: The villages of the Desh are full of able men who would be more than willing to serve in our armies. Let us recruit the $marathi_language$-speaking members of our population into our military.

name: $mhr_ashta_pradhan$
description: $mhr_ashta_pradhan_desc$

name: Office of the Peshwa
description: The #italic Peshwa#! Shall be our chief minister, entirely devoted to both civil administration and overseeing military operations. This consolidation of power will make us versatile enough to expand quickly and efficiently.

name: Forts of Maharashtra
description: In these hilly and densely forested lands, maintaining a series of forts is an offensive necessity as well as a defensive one. Meticulous maintenance of our fortifications should therefore be a top priority.

name: Encourage Brāhmaṇa Ties
description: Our financial sector is dominated by Brāhmaṇa banking families. Let us integrate them further in our administration by hiring them as tax collectors, and creating regulations to strengthen their rights and protect their traditions. We will have gained the favor of our financiers as well as access to learned and able administrators.

name: Lo Statuto del Comune
description: Before most of Europe had thought to write its customs down, the cities of our region had already codified their laws, established their councils, and set out the duties of every citizen and magistrate in the pages of the #italic Statuto#!. From Ancona to Viterbo, these documents were revised, contested, and renewed by each generation, creating a living tradition of civic argument that neither feudal lords nor passing conquerors could wholly extinguish. This heritage of written law makes our institutions resilient and our burghers invested in the city they help to govern.

name: Head of the Church
description: The Bishop of Rome holds a position unlike any other in Christendom — not merely the highest-ranking prelate but the #italic Vicarius Christi#!, whose pronouncements on matters of faith bind every Catholic ruler and kingdom whether they welcome them or not. We cultivate this authority as much through spiritual relationship as through institutional power, presenting ourselves as the father of all the faithful rather than simply their ecclesiastical superior, which gives rivals pause before they choose open confrontation with the See of Rome. This dual standing as institutional head and spiritual father generates a continuous religious influence across Europe and makes antagonizing us a costly act for any ruler who depends on the loyalty of Catholic subjects.

name: Fontana Maggiore
description: Before we had painted our greatest canvases or trained our most celebrated condottieri, we had already declared our ambition in water and stone — the #italic Fontana Maggiore#!, sculpted by Nicola and Giovanni Pisano and fed by a new aqueduct the whole commune funded, rising at the heart of Perugia as proof that no city in central Italy was richer, prouder, or more capable of collective ambition. The fountain gathered every saint, every trade good, and every classical virtue into a single monument and said with marble what no charter could say as well. This civic statement draws pilgrims and merchants to our center and tightens our hold over the streets they fill.

name: Duchy of Spoleto
description: We are the inheritors of the great #italic Duchy of Spoleto#!, the Lombard dominion that once stretched from Umbria to the edges of the Mezzogiorno, and where other communes forgot their martial origins we kept the garrison tradition alive in every hilltop tower and every lord's keep across our lands. The memory of that broad territorial authority shapes how our nobility thinks about defense and how our peasants think about obligation, producing a social compact organized around the protection of altitude and stone. This legacy of distributed fortification and soldierly culture gives our armies a discipline and our territory a resilience that no city-state built from trade alone can match.

name: Studio Generale
description: The university at Perugia, founded in 1308, placed itself under civic rather than ecclesiastical authority, and the schools that followed across our region trained the lawyers, notaries, and administrators who carried the business of the Italian commune forward. Our cities offered the libraries, the patronage, and the debating culture that drew men of learning from across the peninsula, making legal and philosophical training as natural a product of central Italy as any craft. This tradition of learned governance gives our officials a preparation in law and argument that their counterparts in more purely feudal regions struggle to match.

name: The Word of the Lord
description: When the Papacy speaks in matters of faith and governance, it speaks with an authority that no secular ruler can claim — the force of divine mandate expressed through the #italic Bulla Papalis#!, a formal pronouncement that carries the weight of scripture to every Catholic court in Europe. We reinforce this with a legal tradition that stretches back to the donation of imperial authority itself, giving us not only the prestige of God's representative but the documented right to intervene in secular affairs, sanction wars, and call the powerful to account before a higher court than any king commands. This standing as both spiritual voice and legal arbiter means that when we recognize a cause as just, allies gather faster and rivals hesitate longer than they would for any purely secular power.

name: School of the Perugino
description: Pietro Vannucci — the #italic Perugino#! — built the most admired workshop in Umbria within our walls, and his students fanned across Italy carrying the grace of the Umbrian style wherever commissions took them. Raphael came here to learn at his feet before Rome claimed the greater man, and the city that taught the teacher of Raphael carries an artistic reputation no rival in our region can easily dismiss. This tradition of workshop teaching and intensive apprenticeship makes our city a magnet for painters, patrons, and the steady flow of commissions that follows wherever skilled hands gather.

name: Lippi Frescoes
description: We invited Filippo Lippi to paint the apse of our cathedral, and what he gave us was the #italic Stories of the Virgin#! — one of the most luminous and tender fresco cycles of the fifteenth century, left unfinished only by his death in Spoleto itself, where he was buried with honors in the church he had transformed. His tomb in our cathedral turned a patronage arrangement into a permanent pilgrimage point for the cultivated and curious across all of Italy. This artistic legacy deepens our intellectual reputation and draws the learned visitors whose presence sharpens the quality of inquiry throughout our city.

name: Bastioni e Rocche
description: The Italian Wars proved that medieval curtain walls could not stop artillery for more than a morning, and our hill towns responded by turning their greatest natural asset — the ridge, the spur, the ravine — into systems of angled bastions and compact #italic Rocche#! that made each town a distinct tactical problem. Architects and military engineers rebuilt our defenses in stone and rammed earth, positioning artillery platforms at the angles that most terrified attacking batteries. This tradition of fortification adapted to terrain makes our territories harder to overrun and far costlier for any invader to hold.

name: Glory of $rome$
description: The great popes of our age have transformed #italic Roma#! from a city of medieval ruins into the most magnificent court in Christendom — commissioning artists, architects, and scholars to fill the Vatican with beauty that will outlast any dynasty and draw the eyes of Europe to the Apostolic See. We build on the bones of the ancient empire deliberately, wrapping our spiritual authority in the prestige of classical civilization and ensuring that every ambassador who enters our city understands he is visiting a power with roots older than any kingdom he serves. This investment in permanent magnificence means our prestige does not diminish with the passing of individual popes, because what we have built speaks for itself long after the man who commissioned it is gone.

name: The Griffin Companies
description: Our city's emblem is the #italic Griffin#!, and nowhere has it been carried further than on the banners of the Baglioni condottieri who sold their swords — and won wars — across the length of the peninsula. Perugia produces soldiers the way Florence produces painters — in quantity, at quality, with an instinct for command honed by centuries of factional street-fighting and seasonal raiding. This martial tradition breeds officers who inspire loyalty and soldiers who hold their nerve when less experienced men break.

name: Ponte delle Torri
description: The ancient #italic Ponte delle Torri#! — part Roman aqueduct, part fortified bridge — strides across the Tessino gorge on ten great piers, giving us control of the main Apennine passage between Umbria and the Marche. Merchants who wish to cross the mountains must cross our bridge, and we have never been reluctant to collect what that privilege is worth in tolls, intelligence, and deference. This structure makes our territory a natural chokepoint, pulling trade inward and making any would-be aggressor calculate the cost of that crossing before they march.

name: Baroque Sacred Patronage
description: The religious upheavals of the age demanded a visual response, and our cities answered with an explosion of chapels, altarpieces, and sacred facades that transformed every urban skyline into a theatre of piety. Confraternities, civic councils, and wealthy patrons competed to commission the most luminous images, the most dynamic sculptures, and the most persuasive devotional paintings their treasuries could afford. This tradition of sacred patronage sustains our artists, fills our streets with devotional imagery, and signals to every visitor that our culture lives at the center of a confident and expressive spiritual life.

name: Centralize the States
description: The Council of Trent has reformed doctrine and sharpened the institutional boundaries of the Church, but the Papal States themselves remain a patchwork of cities, lordships, and client territories whose local princes have long treated our authority as negotiable. We act now to close that gap — absorbing the revenues, appointments, and legal jurisdictions that local lords have quietly accumulated over generations, and placing them under direct administration from Rome in the manner that the reformed #italic Curia#! demands. This consolidation of crown authority over our territories gives the Papacy the financial and administrative foundation that the Counter-Reformation's ambitions require.

name: Guerra del Sale
description: When the Pope imposed his salt monopoly, our people took up whatever weapons lay to hand — hence the papal mockery that named our uprising the #italic Guerra delle Forche#!, the War of the Forks. We lost that war and were humiliated — the Baglioni expelled, the Rocca Paolina built directly over their palaces as a stone declaration of contempt — yet the defeat calcified into something more durable than pride. This bone-deep suspicion of outside authority makes every Perugian hill a natural fortress and every invader understand that whatever they take from us will cost more to hold than any strategic advantage can justify.

name: Cardinal's Bulwark
description: Cardinal Albornoz built the #italic Rocca Albornoziana#! not as a gesture but as a declaration — a fortress of such impregnability that every petty lord between Rome and Perugia understood that central power had returned in earnest, and that Spoleto stood as its most fortified instrument in central Italy. We have inherited both the structure and the institutional role it embodies, maintaining our city as the most orderly and disciplined administrative center in the region through every upheaval of the age. This combination of military solidity and civic order keeps our population unified, our burgher class literate in their civic duties, and our walls resistant to the storms of revolt and rebellion that trouble less well-governed territories.

name: The Jubilee Economy
description: The Holy Years that Rome declared every quarter-century brought pilgrims from every corner of Latin Christendom onto the roads of our territory, and the #italic Grand Tour#! that followed brought a second wave of wealthy and curious northerners willing to pay generously for comfort, guidance, and company. Our inns, markets, and workshops learned to serve an international clientele, and the money they left behind flowed through every level of our economy. This tradition of hosting the faithful and the curious makes our cities prosperous far beyond what local production alone could sustain.

name: Ecclesiastical Primacy
description: The Peace of Westphalia has excluded us from the diplomacy of princes, but it has not settled the question of who speaks for the Catholic Church within each Catholic kingdom — a question now pressed with dangerous urgency by those who would make the Church a department of the crown. We assert our primacy over the bishops of France, Germany, and Austria not as a formality but as a living doctrinal reality, condemning the propositions of #italic Gallicanism#! and forcing clergy who have drifted toward national loyalties to account for the authority they owe to Rome. This reassertion of the Pope's exclusive right to define Catholic doctrine brings wavering churches back under the orthodoxy of the Holy See and restores the flow of tithes and ecclesiastical revenues that national rulers had begun to redirect toward themselves.

name: Umbrian Academies
description: Long after our political independence was absorbed into the Papal States, the #italic Accademia del Disegno#! and the learned societies we maintained under papal patronage kept our intellectual and artistic culture alive — training the officials, theorists, and artists who staffed institutions far beyond our own borders. Every great power on the peninsula knew that Perugian training produced reliable men, and the steady demand for our graduates made our academies prosperous even as our political leverage diminished. This tradition of practical learned culture sharpens every instrument of governance we exercise and ensures our city punches above its political weight in the councils that matter.

name: Spoletine Silk
description: The mulberry groves of our valley have fed silkworms that supplied the finest weavers in the Papal States for centuries, and the resulting #italic Spoletine silk#! reached the altars of Rome and the wardrobes of courts as far as France and the Habsburgs. Our merchants built a prosperous burgher class on the back of this trade — one with enough surplus to educate its children and enough political sense to keep the guild networks running through every succession of papal governors. This luxury craft tradition fills our treasury from foreign demand and sustains the middling commercial class whose stability is the surest foundation of our peace.

name: Enlightenment Civic Reform
description: The rationalist currents of the eighteenth century found in our communal tradition a soil already prepared to receive them — cities long accustomed to debating their own governance, recording their decisions, and holding their magistrates to account in writing. Reform-minded governors and learned academies pushed for clearer codes, more orderly urban plans, and more predictable administration across the towns and countryside we govern. This embrace of rational governance makes our institutions more efficient and our subjects more inclined to see the state as a partner in civic life rather than an obstacle to it.

name: The Concordat System
description: The political earthquakes of revolution and war have stripped away much of our temporal power, yet the fundamental need of states for religious legitimacy has not diminished — and it is precisely this need that we leverage in the formal treaties we call #italic Concordats#!. We negotiate with each sovereign power separately, trading some degree of independence in administrative matters for legally binding recognition of Church rights, the security of our seminaries, and the formal standing of Catholic clergy within their borders. This system of bilateral agreements transforms every Catholic state from a potential adversary into a partner bound by treaty, giving us a diplomatic reach that no army could have preserved.

name: The Old University
description: When revolution swept across Italy, our ancient university responded not by retreating into its medieval privileges but by opening its doors to the sons of merchants and artisans who would carry the new politics forward. The faculty of the #italic Università degli Studi di Perugia#! produced the lawyers and pamphlet writers who made the Risorgimento possible in Umbria, turning a scholastic institution into an engine of civic transformation. This capacity to translate learning into organization means that no reform our government wishes to pursue will lack for educated men who know how to carry it out.

name: Vale of Spoleto
description: The broad agricultural valley cradled between our hills has been the material foundation of our prosperity since antiquity, and we have spent the revolutionary era improving it — drainage canals, systematic crop rotation, and the redistribution of marginal land into productive holdings that sustain our laboring population through the economic shocks that less prepared states cannot absorb. The #italic Vale of Spoleto#! now feeds our city, supplies our markets with surplus, and generates the agricultural capital that any serious industrial ambition requires as its foundation. This inherited fertility, carefully tended and rationally improved, turns every season into a buffer against the disruptions that ruin neighbors who have spent their resources on less durable investments.

name: Mercantile Spirit
description: $NAP$, inspired by the influential maritime republic of Amalfi, boasts a vibrant culture of trade. Strategic ports, including the city of $naples$ itself, served as vital hubs, connecting the kingdom to distant lands and fostering economic prosperity through commercial exchanges and the flourishing exchange of goods and ideas.

name: The University of $NAP$
description: Founded in 1224 by Emperor Frederick II, the University of $NAP$ is one of $ITA$'s oldest public institutions. Embracing a secular ethos, it has provided generations of students with a comprehensive education and contributed to intellectual advancements across various fields.

name: The Royal Domain
description: We have inherited a wealthy realm, but we have been stymied from achieving true prosperity by the constraints of archaic laws and customs. Previous rulers balanced noble privilege with economic power, but we must bring attitude and regulations into the modern era. By strengthening courts of the nobility and consolidating their landholdings, we will create a clearer legal hierarchy. Simultaneously, we will empower cities as centers of royal authority and encourage the proliferation of urban trade and craftsmanship.

name: Accademia Pontaniana
description: For a long time, $NAP$ has striven to be a center of modern learning, attracting the great minds of the age and spreading the light of the $renaissance$. Under the leadership of Giovanni Pontano, these discussion circles have been given structure and organization. It is only fitting that we name the academy after its industrious leader.

name: Crushed Power of the Barons
description: Local barons still exert a large degree of power over the Neapolitan countryside. If we wish to continue centralizing our kingdom, we must crush the power of these barons, or risk them conspiring against us.

name: Encouraged City Living
description: We have inherited an exquisite city from our predecessors. We must continue to beautify and improve this metropolis of the Mediterranean so that it can continue to grow and prosper. No longer can we content ourselves with merely repairing and maintaining the port and buildings; we shall make holistic improvements that better sustain our people by also building aqueducts, draining wetlands, and paving more roads.

name: City of Artists
description: Through patronage of the world's greatest artists, the glory of our city will become known throughout the world. All will marvel at the greatness of our painters, poets, singers, and actors. Let $NAP_ADJ$ culture be the mark by which other centers of art are measured!

name: Expanded Arsenale
description: For centuries, the Arsenale of $NAP$ has been the center of our ship production and our main naval installation. However, it needs to be expanded and modernized to remain effective against hostile Mediterranean fleets. Let us expand both the commercial and military capabilities of our port, building a more efficient Arsenale to maintain a larger, more powerful fleet.

name: A Central Mediterranean Power
description: Our advantageous central position in the Mediterranean enables effortless access to any shore. We should capitalize on this asset to seek alliances, forge new friendships, and expand our borders. With the sea as our gateway, opportunities abound for growth and prosperity in our quest for greater influence and security.

name: Institutional Reorganization
description: By abolishing the Collateral Council and establishing the #italic Real Camera di Santa Chiara#!, we will implement important legal reforms in $NAP$. Ongoing projects will aim to reorganize the legislative complex, consolidate laws into the #italic Codice Carolino#!, and implement the #italic Onciario Cadastre#! for tax reform.

name: $NAP_ADJ$ Army Reforms
description: Our nation needs to undergo sweeping military reforms, modernizing its armed forces to meet the challenges of the changing battlefield. These reforms will bolster tactical capabilities, streamline command structures, and enhance training programs, positioning us as a formidable force in our region.

name: $NAP_ADJ$ Industrialization
description: $NAP$ has witnessed a gradual industrialization process over the past decades. Key sectors such as textiles, shipbuilding, and ironworks have experienced significant growth, fueled by investments and technological advancements. This shift towards industrialization will play a significant role in transforming $NAP$ into a major economic center.

name: Children of the Himalayas
description: Our people have lived since time immemorial in the shadow of very mountains that sustain the Heavens. The high passes, the steep ridgelines, the deep-cut river valleys — these are not obstacles to us but the very fabric of our homeland. Even the air itself is different than that of the lowlands, and no army from the plains can expect to move through these lands as our soldiers do.

name: The Divya Upadesh
description: The #italic Divya Upadesh#! lays out nine principles that form the core of political and national life in $nepal_area$, as well as guidelines for successful foreign policy. It encapsulates centuries of $nepali_group$ thought on governance, war, and peace. Following these principles, $nepal_area$ shall be able to avoid the subversion of nearby empires and marauding foreigners.

name: $a_gurkha$
description: $a_gurkha_desc$

name: $flemish_cloth_industries_right$
description: $flemish_cloth_industries_right_desc$

name: Polders
description: The Low Countries are highly susceptible to flooding, and the many disastrous floods that happened between the 11th and 14th centuries led to the creation of the Zuiderzee. This excessive flooding also caused coastal soils to become uselessly salinated. Thankfully, we now have the technology to reclaim this damaged land and use it productively for agriculture.

name: $NED_ADJ$ Shipbuilding
description: As the Low Countries are home to some of $europe$'s greatest port cities, it is only fitting that they should also boast some of $europe$'s greatest shipyards. Being able to employ skilled local craftsmen dramatically reduces the costs of acquiring new merchant fleets.

name: Nomadic Legacy
description: Our people are born in the saddle, free to roam the world without the need to put down roots.

name: The Ricèt
description: Specially linked to the Piedmontese countryside, villages have traditionally developed the #italic Ricetto#! (in standard Italian and Ricèt in Piedmontese) — a fortified area within the town used to store the community's grain and wine and provide refuge during raids. This is not a lord's castle, but a communal asset managed by the villagers. This has allowed the peasantry to survive the frequent wars between the various nations of the area, ensuring that the state's productive capacity remains intact even during invasions.

name: The Paleologue Dynasty
description: The ancient blood of the #italic Paleologue#! gives our marquisate a dignity and legitimacy that commands respect from the greatest courts of Europe. This lineage connects us to a world of ceremony and diplomacy that most smaller states can only admire from afar. We carry this heritage as a shield as much as an ornament, using it to open doors that our armies alone could never unlock.

name: The Piedmontese Ordinance
description: For generations, our mountain lords levied troops on custom and season, calling men to arms when the harvest was done and sending them home before the first snow. We have replaced this improvised tradition with a formal ordinance that fixes the size, equipment, and training standards of our infantry and binds our cities and rural lords to consistent obligations that can be called on at any time. This #italic Ordinansa Piemontèisa#! (#italic Ordinanza Piemontese#! in standard Italian: Piedmontese Ordinance) gives our army a professional core that holds its cohesion between campaigns, advancing the discipline and tradition of arms that lesser levies can never maintain.

name: Le fere dël Piemont
description: The Piedmontese cities have been formalizing great trade fairs across the region. By providing state protection and tax exemptions for international merchants, the state will turn the Alpine crossings into corridors of wealth. This will bring us riches, providing the necessary funds to purchase the loyalty of independent lords.

name: Casale Monferrato
description: We have made #italic Casale Monferrato#! the heart of our state, a city that grows in commerce and craft under the shelter of our rule. The merchants and guilds of the city bring life to its streets and revenues to our treasury, and its position on the roads between great powers makes it a natural gathering place for trade. This city is our richest possession and the proof of what sound governance can build.

name: The Piedmontese Cavalry
description: The plains of the Po where they open onto our territory have long supported a class of lesser noble horsemen whose wealth depended on the quality of their horses and the reputation of their lance arm. We have organized these scattered men-at-arms into a formal cavalry, standardizing their equipment and training in coordinated maneuver rather than the individual charge that served in an earlier age. This #italic Cavalleria Piemontese#! can screen our flanks, pursue a broken enemy, and fight in the loose formations that modern battlefield conditions demand, giving our armies a mobility that infantry alone cannot provide.

name: The Piassafòrt
description: Recognizing our position as the gateway to Italy, we will begin transforming our cities into #italic Piassafòrt#! (Fortress-Cities). This will require a cultural reinforcement toward living under constant threat, where city planning is dictated by the needs of artillery and garrisons. This engineering excellence will make Piedmont the most difficult region in Italy to conquer, forcing foreign powers to negotiate rather than invade.

name: The Court Culture
description: Our court has become a gathering place for artists, scholars, and musicians drawn by the patronage and refined taste we offer. We prize the #italic Arts of the Court#! as instruments of prestige, and the works produced under our roof reflect well on our name wherever they travel. This investment in culture returns in reputation what it costs in coin.

name: The Via delle Gallie
description: The ancient road descending from the Alpine passes into the Po plain once carried the legions of Rome; it has never ceased to carry merchants, envoys, and armies for whom the Piedmontese corridor is the most direct route between Italy and the north. We invest in the maintenance and security of these roads, building waypoints and toll stations that bring reliable revenue and ensure that goods in transit can move faster through our territory than through any rival route. This control over the #italic Via d'le Gàlie#! (#italic Via delle Gallie#! in standard Italian: Road of the Gauls) makes us an indispensable link in the chain of European commerce, increasing the capacity of our markets and giving our envoys natural openings at the courts that depend on the roads we manage.

name: The Nebbiolo Vigne
description: While cultivated since antiquity, we will implement a scientific approach to viticulture in the vineyards of our region. By supporting the modernization and standardization of the vineyards and regulating the production of high-value wines (Nebbiolo), the state will ensure a luxury export that generates massive trade revenue. These measures will provide the treasury with a stable income that is immune to the fluctuations of the grain market.

name: The Casale Citadel
description: We have transformed #italic Casale Monferrato#! into a fortress city whose walls and bastions are among the most formidable in the peninsula. The citadel's deep ditches and angled walls are designed to exhaust any siege and bleed any attacker who thinks to take it quickly. This fortification has made our seat of power into one of the great military prizes of the age, too costly to assault and too important to ignore.

name: The Citadel System
description: A generation of engineers trained on the latest Italian treatises on fortification has surveyed every significant town in our domain and begun the work of converting the old circuit walls into a network of modern bastions — angled, low, and wide enough to mount artillery while denying the enemy any approach that our own guns cannot cover. We tie these citadels together by road and signal, so that a garrison threatened in one valley can expect support from the next. This #italic Sistema delle Cittadelle#! transforms Piedmont into a country that cannot be overrun but must be taken fortress by fortress, a prospect that gives even the most determined aggressor pause before crossing our borders.

name: The Canal
description: Our administration will undertake a titanic effort to tame the waters of our main rivers: the Po, the Dora, and the Sesia. By constructing an intricate network of stone canals and sluices, we will transform the flooded plains and abundant marshes into the most productive rice and grain fields in Southern Europe. This will provide the region with a massive, reliable food surplus, allowing the population to grow and sustain a permanent standing army unaffected by foreign grain imports.

name: The Marquisate's Resilience
description: We have survived between greater powers through the arts of flexibility and careful friendship, never placing our trust entirely in any single alliance. By maintaining a reputation for reasonableness and good faith, we have made ourselves useful to those who might otherwise simply absorb us. This #italic Diplomatic Resilience#! is our oldest strategy and our most reliable one.

name: The Enlightened Court
description: The generation of reformers who have gathered around our court have convinced us that the task of government is not merely to preserve what exists but to discover what works better and systematically replace the old with the new. We open our administration to men trained in the academies and experimental societies of the age, commission reports on everything from agricultural yields to judicial procedure, and fund the education of a class of administrators who can read a budget as readily as a treaty. This #italic Còrt Ëluminà#! (#italic Corte Illuminata#! in standard Italian: Enlightened Court) produces a state whose institutions are continuously improved by reason rather than paralyzed by custom, making our government faster, our research more productive, and our subjects more literate.

name: The Setajòj
description: Piedmont will become the silk capital of Europe, characterized by massive silk factories (Filatoi) that will utilize advanced hydraulic machinery. This will create an early industrial culture in our towns, where a new class of technical artisans and merchants will emerge. These investments will provide the region with the capital needed to fund modern infrastructure and military upgrades, linking the Piedmontese economy directly to the global market.

name: The Monferrato Agricoltura
description: The rolling hills and fertile valleys of our marquisate yield harvests that sustain our people and support a growing population of farmers and rural craftsmen. Through careful management and investment in our lands, we have expanded the reach of our agriculture into slopes and terraces that once lay idle. This #italic Agricultural Transformation#! brings new settlers to our countryside and new revenues to our state.

name: The Industrial Base
description: The combination of water power from our mountain rivers, a growing population of skilled artisans in our cities, and the raw materials of the Alpine foothills has created the conditions for an early industrial transformation that no other region of Italy can yet match. We invest in the hydraulic mills, the standardized workshops, and the credit institutions that allow this productive base to expand systematically rather than grow by accident. This #italic Base Industriale#! generates income from activities that were once invisible to the treasury and draws workers from the countryside into our towns, building the urban population and the taxable wealth of our state together.

name: Breadbasket of $india$
description: The five great rivers — Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, and Sutley — penetrate the lands of the $punjab_area$ area, granting the soil the blessing of unmatched fertility. Apart from allowing us to export food and cotton to our neighbors, this also allows our many cities to grow and encourages all sorts of specialized production. We must do our utmost to encourage the growth of agriculture and to defend our farmers from the bandits and brigands in the adjoining areas.

name: Encourage Indo-Persian Trade
description: Situated on the westernmost border of $india$, the $PUN$ has always been at the crossroads of economic and cultural exchange between $india$ and $persia_region$. The ancient Grand Trunk Road, which connects eastern $india$ to the $farsi_culture$ world, runs right through our lands before heading up into the Afghan mountain passes. These passes are, however, plagued by tribal raiders and bandits. We should encourage the traffic along this ancient and vibrant route and do everything in our power to look after the wellbeing of these traders by constructing caravanserais and policing these roads.

name: Gurmukhī Script
description: The Gurmukhī script is an #italic abugida#! developed in the lands of $PUN$, and is highly favored by our $sikhism_ADJ$ gurus. Our clergy is using this script in order to record $sikhism_ADJ$ texts.

name: The Khalsa
description: $sikhism$, a religion native to the $PUN$, is spreading rapidly in our lands. Members of this faith come from all castes and backgrounds, and will defend their state regardless of their former professions.

name: $PUN_ADJ$ Textile Industry
description: The $PUN$ is a major center for textile production. $cloth$ from our weavers is specially made for markets all over $asia$ and $europe$, and our weavers are among the most productive in $india$.

name: Strength of the Misls
description: The administrative system of the Misl states of $PUN$ allows them to field impressive cavalry forces. In times of need, we may call upon these forces to fight a common enemy.

name: Reforming the $PUN_ADJ$ Army
description: The ways of our forefathers were sound, and have served us well over the years. But in order for our armies to continue to triumph on the battlefields, we must create a more professional military. By studying the way other countries organize their armies and adapting their methods when prudent, we may create a more efficient $PUN_ADJ$ army while still retaining the unique qualities of our current military system.

name: Militaristic Society
description: There is almost no division between civil and military society among the Rajputs. Our nation is a host, defined by its people rather than by the land we control, and its people are warriors. We must ensure that military divisions properly meet our administrative needs as the host expands.

name: Combat Training
description: Every soldier is trained for battle, but our people start combat training at a much younger age, granting them skills surpassing those of other green soldiers.

name: Clan Loyalties
description: The influence of our clan extends far beyond our own borders. We are able to draw from other Rajput groups from all over northern $india$ when filling the ranks of our armies.

name: Monumental Architecture
description: What purpose does victory serve if there is nothing to immortalize our achievements? Monuments, such as an awe-inspiring Tower of Victory, shall be erected, so future generations will know of our greatest battles and be appropriately inspired.

name: Marwari Horses
description: Like their masters, Rajput cavalry horses are meticulously trained to perform on the field of battle. It is said that a Marwari horse will only leave the battlefield under one of three conditions - victory, death, or when carrying a wounded master to safety. By taking good care of these divine beings, we will ensure the everlasting dominance of our horsemen on the battlefields of $india$.

name: Reorganized Rajput Regiments
description: Traditional clan structures are an excellent foundation for a modernized regimental system. Existing hierarchies based on kinship and unconditional loyalty can be easily translated into an organized and formal chain of command.

name: Martial Smiths
description: Wars are not only won through tactics and bravery, but also through weaponry. Our blacksmiths shall forge the finest martial weapons for our warriors to wield in defense of the Rajput people.

name: Fortress Architecture
description: The rise of $DLH$, and the invading $muslim_ADJ$ warriors of the past, were wake-up calls. We must always be prepared for foreign invaders, and thus, we must hire the most skilled architects to design impregnable forts throughout our realm. The immensely long walls that will be needed to protect our land make this an ambitious project, but our determination to defend our people shall ensure that it is done.

name: Expanded Artillery Arm
description: Sieges are what win wars. We must experiment with ways of creating bigger and better cannons to bring down the many forts of our enemies, both within $india$ and outside it.

name: The Purbias
description: The Rajputs have spread themselves throughout northern $india$ in their pursuit of glory. The #italic Purbias#!, elite Rajput soldiers who venture as mercenaries, are renowned for their combat ability, and as such spread our fearsome reputation.

name: Mandatory Firearm Drills
description: Many Rajput soldiers are experts in the use of personal firearms. We should put these hardened veterans to work training the next generation of soldiers, rather than risking the loss of their expertise in battle. All of our soldiers must be drilled in firearms tactics before they are expected to meet our enemies on the front line.

name: Rajput Painting School
description: Rajput painters already have an excellent reputation, but it could be even better. We must encourage our artists to develop their skills and add to the glory of our dynasty by creating a school of painting particular to our state.

name: Rajput Resistance
description: Rajput poet-musicians tell stories of our people's many battles against foreign invaders, and how our ancestors would rather die than admit themselves defeated. We must encourage this spirit of unity, and give our musicians reason to write new ballads of bravery in the face of death.

name: Martial Ethos
description: The upbringing and traditions of Rajput warriors ensure a wide base for recruiting officers to lead our armies. In order to capitalize on this, we should formalize career opportunities and advancement paths to encourage these promising young fighters to serve as officers in our forces.

name: Al Téri dl'Esarchét
description: Romagna has preserved a unique legal artifact of the Byzantine Exarchate of Ravenna. Unlike the Lombard-influenced north, Romagnol culture has retained a deeper layer of Roman-Byzantine administrative law. This has fostered a differentiated culture, where even the smallest towns claim ancient imperial privileges. This administrative complexity makes the region a nightmare for large empires to centralize efficiently, as every valley is protected by its own Roman web of exemptions and local statutes.
