description: We have been the #italic Shugo#! of Bungo since the $kamakura$ era. These lands are known for their highly fertile soil, and the rich harvests from this region allow us to feed larger armies than many other $daimyo$ can support.

name: Descendants of Baekje
description: Our chronicle says we are descendants of Prince Imseong of the royal house of the ancient Baekje Kingdom, which once ruled in $korea_region$. This legendary connection means we hold a prestigious position in $east_asia$.

name: $hitachi_province$ Genji
description: We are one of the oldest Minamoto lines in the Kantō region, and have fought for our clan's glory in eastern $japan_region$ since before Minamoto no Yoritomo founded the $kamakura$ Shogunate. Our position as #italic Shugo#! of $hitachi_province$ is therefore never in question.

name: Multiple Shugo
description: We have been made #italic Shugo#! of multiple provinces. Administering all this land will make us rich from revenue generated by our fertile rice paddies and the workshops of the region's most skilled artisans.

name: $satsuma_province$ Shugo
description: We have always traditionally held the title of #italic Shugo#! of $satsuma_province$; its name has become synonymous with our clan. Our warriors are proud of this, and therefore always ready to defend our territory.

name: Vice-Minister of Dazaifu
description: As the name of our clan shows, we come from the appointed vice minister of the Dazaifu in $chikuzen_province$ province. This institution has since antiquity been the diplomatic and military center of the region, and we traditionally govern Northern Kyūshū as representative of the Emperor.

name: Wakō Tradition
description: While we appreciate lawful and peaceful trade, we also need to be prepared for tense military situations. Fortunately, the local tradition of piracy could help us solve certain combat-related issues.

name: $kai_province$ Shugo
description: We are descendants of the Genji of $kai_province$, and have been traditionally appointed as its #italic Shugo#!. As such, we are intrinsically associated with it, and the famous horses from the province are already synonymous with our cavalry.

name: Genji of $mino_province$
description: As the head of the Genji in $mino_province$ and its appointed #italic Shugo#!, we have led other local samurai for generations. Our domain occupies an advantageous position from which to control the neighboring regions.

name: Strong Dynastic Ties
description: Our family descends from the prestigious line of the $fujiwara_dynasty$, and we also have strong ties to the $ashikaga_dynasty$, as the mother of $ashikaga_dynasty$ Takauji was a member of our clan. These dynastic ties will prove invaluable for our prosperity.

name: $fujiwara_dynasty$ Descendants
description: Our genealogy shows that the ancestors of our clan were originally members of the $fujiwara_dynasty$ family from $kyoto$. This kinship to such an ancient and revered dynasty is very useful for making diplomatic connections to the Imperial Court and with the other clans.

name: Descendants of the $nitta_dynasty$
description: We are descendants of the $nitta_dynasty$ clan, ancient rivals of the $ashikaga_dynasty$ family. To some this is proof of the depths of our loyalty, while to others this makes us a natural enemy. We must cleverly utilize our lineage as a diplomatic weapon.

name: Emerging Clan
description: Despite our impressive ancestry, our clan is very new, as our split from the Sasaki clan is relatively recent. Our people are eager to prove their worth as scions of an independent name.

name: $ezo_area$ Kanrei
description: The position of the $ezo_area$ #italic Kanrei#!, or administrator of $ezo_area$, has been assigned to our clan since the time of the $kamakura$ Shogunate. We are in charge of managing the island as a place of exile for criminals, necessitating constant communication across the strait.

name: Control of $buddhist_ADJ$ Sects
description: $echizen_province$ is home to many important temples representing different sects, such as the Eiheiji of the Sōtō tradition and the Heisenji of the Tendai tradition, among others. If we could bring all of them under our control and establish religious peace throughout the province, it would be the foundation of an ideal religious policy for our entire nation.

name: Dream of Masakado
description: $taira_dynasty$ no Masakado, a great warrior and close kinsman of our clan, once tried to become the Emperor of Eastern $japan_region$. Sadly, Masakado could not fulfill his ambition, but his dream of founding a new nation of samurai should be our guiding star.

name: God of the Arts
description: The ancestral founder of our clan, Hata no Kawakatsu, was highly admired as the patron god of all art, from traditional dances to theater. Our clan must live up to his legacy if we are to earn the respect we deserve.

name: Ōshū Shugo
description: As an honorable clan dating back to the early $kamakura$ period, we have a strong claim to rule over the entire Ōshū province. Fortunately for us, what land Ōshū exactly covers is not well-defined.

name: Shogunate Ties
description: As a clan descending from one of the branches of the $ashikaga_dynasty$, we have particularly strong ties to the authority of the Shogunate. As long as we maintain this association, our clan will continue to be held in high regard.

name: Branches and Retainers
description: Our widespread clan controls rich territories through a network of loyal kinsmen and retainers. By maintaining internal harmony in our dynasty, our clan will become one of the most powerful in $JAP$.

name: Claim to the Shogunate
description: As our clan is descended from the $ashikaga_dynasty$ family, we have a strong claim on the position of $JAPANESE_SHOGUNATE_LEADER_MALE$, should the main line perish. Even if the Bakufu is not threatened, it would still be in our best interests to remind everyone of our legitimacy. Just in case it ever becomes relevant...

name: Minister of Samurai-Dokoro
description: We are one of four powerful clans traditionally appointed to be the chief of military and police in the Samurai-Dokoro. It is thus our responsibility, and our privilege, to keep the peace in the capital and other important places.

name: Resistance Against Invasions
description: Our contributions to defending the country against the $MGE_ADJ$ invasions are well known. Kikuchi Takefusa's achievements in repelling the invaders are widely lauded, and all our troops aim to fight as bravely as him.

name: Control of $ise_province$
description: From the wealthy south to the densely populated urban north, we have extended our control over the entire province of $ise_province$. This will allow us to fully exploit provincial resources to further the growth of our clan's influence.

name: Blessing of Amaterasu
description: As the keepers of the holiest of $japan_region$'s shrines at $ise_province$, we are blessed by Amaterasu, goddess of the sun and the universe. We must rise to be worthy of the task of maintaining and caring for this national treasure, which will earn us the respect of the $japanese_group$ people.

name: Rule Over the Inland Sea
description: The Seto Inland Sea has a special importance for trade routes of $japan_region$, and maintaining naval dominance here could make or break our clan. We must ensure that we always have a strong navy with which to control maritime trade.

name: Fighting Famine
description: Due to cold winds in the late autumn and heavy snows until the early spring, our people often suffer from severe famines and hunger. We must build reserves of food and look into how we can improve the lands under our control to counter future catastrophes.

name: $shinano_province$ Shugo
description: Our clan belongs to a sub-branch of the Minamoto, and rules $shinano_province$ Province as its #italic Shugo#!. Our land is mountainous and unwelcoming to many. For our people, however, it has for a long time been an integrated part of our defenses against outsiders. Let us take this experience with us wherever our armies go, and make sure to always obtain thorough information about the terrain in any region where we do battle.

name: Suwa Taisha
description: Suwa Taisha at Lake Suwa is one of the oldest shrines in $japan_region$, and highly adored throughout the country. Its most important festival, #italic Onbashira-matsuri#!, proves the bravery of our people as they carry the sacred logs from the mountain to the shrine.

name: Domination of Kyūshū
description: We have been designated #italic Shugo#! of $bungo_province$, $hizen_province$, and $hyuuga_province$. This positions us perfectly to claim all of Kyūshū for ourselves!

name: Trade with $korea_region$
description: Due to our location, we are the clan trading most actively with $korea_region$, and as a result we have a near-monopoly on many exotic goods. We must do what we can to retain this favorable position, and leverage it to out-compete any upstart that might challenge us.

name: $kashima_shrine$
description: $kashima_shrine$ is one of three most important shrines in the Kantō region. This shrine is dedicated to Takemikazuchi-no-O-no-Kami, who is the god of thunder and swords, and also the patron god of $sumo$ wrestling. Our custodianship of this shrine strengthens the resolve of our armies.

name: Ōshū Ties
description: Ōshū Province is our second home and where our clan originated. We must make use of our ties to Ōshū to procure some of the strong war horses native to that region.

name: Defender of $JAP$
description: As a prominent samurai family from Northern Kyūshū, we have bravely fought against both $MGE_ADJ$ invasions. Should the need arise, we will once again rise to defend both Kyūshū and the realm at large from outside invaders.

name: Fight for Tsushima
description: Lying between $asia$ and the islands of $japan_region$, our homeland of $tsushima_province$ and its surrounding waters are where countries clash and fight hard. May our own fleets be strong, so that we can not only defend our country, but also expand it!

name: Takeda-Ryū
description: Traditional forms of martial arts have been practiced in our family for generations. Among them, there is particular emphasis on horse riding and mounted archery, making our mounted troops much more effective soldiers than those from other clans.

name: Bellflower Banner
description: Having been its Shugo for generations, our emblem is already synonymous with $mino_province$. All who live there will fight under our banner.

name: Double Shugo
description: We have been appointed #italic Shugo#! of both $kouzuke_province$ and $tango_province$ Provinces. Their plentiful lands are the perfect starting point for our expansion.

name: Legacy of Nasu no Yoichi
description: $shimotsuke_province$ was once the home of Nasu no Yoichi, who was famous for his abilities as an archer during the Genpei War. To this day, the warriors of $shimotsuke_province$ hold him in high regard; we are proud to be called 'the best archers in Kantō' and to carry on Nasu no Yoichi's legacy.

name: Succession Dispute Mediation
description: As many of the other clans squabble within themselves over who is the rightful heir to whom, they turn to us to mediate their disputes. Doing so puts us in a unique position of power and trust, making it easy for us to make new allies and contacts — and to destabilize our rivals.

name: $ainu_culture$ Trade
description: We are among the first $japanese_group$ to have established permanent trade with the $ainu_culture$. Our ships go back and forth between their lands and ours, greatly benefiting both communities.

name: Unification of Shikoku
description: Shikoku is seen as a poor, isolated land by the rest of $japan_region$, where nothing of importance happens. Let them continue thinking that and overlook our unification of the island until it is too late.

name: Control of the $izumi$ Sea
description: Our clan's territory has traditionally been situated around the Kii Channel. Taking control of trade entering the mainland through that point will bring us massive profits, and we shall flourish immensely.

name: Control of the Tōkaidō
description: The Tōkaidō is the most important trade route between Central and Eastern $japan_region$. As our ancestral lands are in the middle of all this trade, it would behoove us to take control over the entire region, so as to reap the most benefits from local commercial activity.

name: March of Kitabatake Akiie
description: Our honorable ancestor Kitabatake Akiie proved that even the long march from $ou_area$ to central $japan_region$ can be undertaken rapidly if one has enough determination. We must learn from this feat and train our armies in swift maneuvering, so that we can quickly move from one front to another as needed.

name: Northern Horses
description: Mutsu has ranches, from which horses were sent to $kyoto$ in ancient times. The tradition of horse farming continues until today, and is one we should cultivate, as it allows us to raise cavalry more easily than many of our neighbors.

name: $ODA$ Generals
description: Obsession with birth and privilege has made this country weak, and the rise of self-made powerful clans throughout the realm has clearly proven how useless such notions can be. Let us take this lesson to heart, and allow success and skill be the guiding principles for who should rise to command our armies. Strong leadership is a requirement for rapid expansion.

name: Kiso-Uma
description: Horses from the Kiso area are our preferred breed. They are not as high nor as fast as other types, but they make up for it with high stamina, and are sturdy enough to survive in the mountains.

name: Welcoming the Nanban Trade
description: Others may denounce foreigners as barbarians, but we recognize the benefits and advantages of trading with them. Let it be known that they will always be welcome in our ports — and we will be able to expand our trade network further than our rivals.

name: Countering Piracy
description: In order to retain good relations with nations on the continent for the sake of our traders, we must mount constant sea patrols. As long as pirates and smugglers are common in our waters, foreigners will not trust us, and may even act against us.

name: $SBA$ Retainers
description: We have talented, but ambitious vassals in our clan. They are a frequent cause of familial friction, and we would be wise to rein them in. Then again, close supervision and lavish, yet strategic rewards could turn these powerful families into the greatest assets of our rule.

name: Tsurinobuse
description: #italic Tsurinobuse#!, 'lure and ambush', is our most effective tactic. This strategy enables us to beat enemies when we are vastly outnumbered, which is of course a very valuable skill. We must make this a central tactic of our armies, and give the dull-witted commanders of rival clans a little surprise.

name: Diplomacy Through Tsushima
description: Thanks to our presence in $tsushima_province$, we have a wealth of experience in negotiating with $korea_region$. This way, we have always been able to keep a channel open to the outside world, even during times when official relations were forbidden.

name: Bahan Ship
description: Our privateer ships fly the flag of Hachiman, spreading terror wherever they go. No one would dare attack a fleet protected by the god of war himself!

name: Flood Control
description: In our home province, the three big rivers of Kiso, Nagara, and Ibi often cause serious flooding in our rice fields. We should control this overflow, and use it to increase the yield in all provinces under our rule.

name: Eastern Power
description: Although we have been granted territory in both eastern and western $japan_region$, it is in the east where we will truly be able to flourish. Our territories there are rich, and we can attract many skilled local warriors to fight for our cause.

name: Mediator of Kantō
description: As one of the oldest clans in Kantō, we have a keen insight into regional politics, and have worked as a mediator between different factions on many occasions. This same comprehensive understanding of our home region allows us to expand our territory effectively without provoking others.

name: The Western Army
description: Let us forge a great western army to unite the squabbling states of $japan_region$. Skillful generals, well-trained soldiers, and ironclad bravery will easily force the Easterners to their knees!

name: Defenders of the Imperial Court
description: When the $kamakura$ Shogunate fell, we were the ones who protected the Emperor and the Imperial Court. This has afforded us a position at the forefront of all clans in $JAP$, as the true protector of the Empire and its courtly traditions.

name: Bugyōshū and Hōkōshū
description: We must strengthen the authority of our administrative officials, such as the Bugyōshū magistrates and the Hōkōshū commanders. A strong bureaucracy can sometimes be the only thing that stands between us and an open civil war.

name: Higashiyama Culture
description: Built around the ascetics of Zen $buddhism$, Higashiyama culture sees beauty in simplicity. It has promoted development of the formal tea ceremony, #italic ikebana#! flower arrangements, theater, and art. This blossoming of culture has brought great prestige to those who practice the arts, and will reflect well upon our realm.

name: Irrigation of Southern Kantō
description: Large parts of our domain is marshland that cannot support intensive agriculture. Recent developments in irrigation technology, however, make it possible to drain marshes and cultivate new arable lands. Let us undertake a grand project of developing these otherwise useless lands; we stand to profit enormously.

name: Expand the Navy
description: $japan_region$ is a nation of islands, and as a result, a strong navy is an absolute necessity. $tosa_province$ is an ideal place to begin building an armada of our own.

name: Dragon of Ōshū
description: Our might and power will be the envy of our enemies. Our name will forever be associated with the Dragon of Ōshū.

name: Clan Spread
description: Our clan is not content to occupy a single location, and we do our utmost to project our influence all over the country. No matter how far it may spread, our clan authority must be unquestionable in all our holdings.

name: Unlikely Alliances
description: Sometimes, the best way to defeat an enemy is to make them your friend. Securing our rule through strategic marriages will not only pacify our foes and gain us new allies, but will also ensure that we can ultimately dominate our rivals through blood.

name: Sympathy for New Faiths
description: Foreigners coming to our land bring with them foreign beliefs. We must of course make sure that this is harmless to our traditional belief systems, but as long as there is no risk to us, we see no reason to disallow people from choosing their own faith.

name: Murakami Suigun
description: The Murakami clan is well-known for committing piracy in the Seto Inland Sea. Let us integrate them fully in our own clan, and send these fearsome privateers after our enemies!

name: Munakata Three Goddesses
description: The three daughters of Susanoo-no-Mikoto are patron goddesses of the sea and navigation. Their blessings will make our navies unstoppable.

name: Tenka Fubu
description: It is clearly our destiny to hold all the country within our grasp. None shall resist our authority, and all under Heaven will bend to our military might.

name: Triple Firing
description: The advent of firearms has and will continue to revolutionize warfare in $japan_region$, and through mastering these new weapons, we can dominate any battlefield. In order to increase the rate of their fire, our arquebusiers will form ranks, allowing one line to fire while two others reload.

name: Improving the Nakasendō
description: The Nakasendō is one of the most important routes between central and eastern $japan_region$. Controlling it also means controlling the trade that flows through it.

name: $christian_ADJ$ Converts
description: Our increasing interactions with foreigners have sparked an interest in $christian$ for many in our clan. The $christian_ADJ$ people have many powerful advocates among our lords and vassals, and few are as zealous as recent converts. Let us make good use of these $christian_ADJ$ converts, regardless of which route our own clan takes, and use their influence and zeal to further our own agenda.

name: Welcome the Westerners
description: As our trade network expands, we come in more frequent contact with foreigners and their strange habits and faiths. Regardless of what they believe, their coin is good enough; we should appear to be open to their ideas as we are to their business if we wish to secure repeat commerce.

name: Eastern Coalitions
description: Regardless of the hostile clans around us, we have always presented ourselves as a reasonable third party for other clans to attach themselves to for protection against invaders. This tradition of eastern coalitions will serve us well, as long as we make sure that the clans who rely on us never have to worry about protection.

name: $SMZ$ Charge
description: Even when surrounded and outnumbered, our soldiers will keep marching forward until they reach the other side of the enemy lines. The charge of our troops will be legendary!

name: Tanegashima Teppō
description: The Westerners who first landed on Tanegashima brought with them new and interesting weapons. These arquebuses are becoming an increasingly common sight all over $japan_region$, but nowhere have they been available for as long as here.

name: Tiger of Kai
description: Strong leaders are better at safeguarding their domains than any number of imposing castles. Our generals must train hard, and earn the right to be called the 'Tiger of Kai'.

name: Fūrinkazan
description: 'Swift like the wind, gentle like the forest, aggressive like fire, immovable like a mountain.' The words of the great war master Sun Tzu shall be permanently etched into our family's history, and shall serve as our motto.

name: Dragon of Echigo
description: Our clan has fostered such an extraordinary spirit of courage and justice that it intimidates our opponents on the battlefield. We will declare the strength of our leaders to all the world, and everyone will quake with terror at the thought of the Dragon of Echigo!

name: Isolated Heartland
description: Our homeland is mountainous and isolated. Fortunately, this also means that any potential conquerors would find our territory almost impossible to reach! Let us build our defenses so that they complement the natural protective strength of our geography — any invader will bitterly regret the day they turned their greedy eyes to our possessions.

name: Shugo System
description: #italic Shugo#! are important vassals for the Shogunate, administrating the lands in name of the $JAPANESE_SHOGUNATE_LEADER_MALE$. Thanks to them, we can administer our lands better and more efficiently.

name: Intensive Domain Development
description: Many dismiss $ou_area$ as poor due to its harsh weather and mountains, yet the region holds great potential. Through infrastructure investment — new towns, waterways, expanded cultivation — and by abolishing stifling tolls and taxes, we can substantially improve our heartland and make our subjects wealthy.

name: March to $kyoto$
description: In these dangerous times when $japan_region$ and $kyoto$ are mired in political chaos, anyone could march into the capital and seize power. As close kinsmen of the $ashikaga_dynasty$, it is our obligation — and our right — to ensure the stability of the country.

name: Influential Strongholds
description: $japan_region$ is a land of castles and fortifications. It is through the construction of strong defensive positions that one can assert influence both over the political realm and the routes vital to military campaigns. This learning is one we must take to heart. It is also through our castles that we impose our presence and power upon the common people. At all times, we must prioritize the reduction of enemy fortifications and the erection of our own in strategic locations.

name: Patronization of the West
description: Western missionaries brought many ideas and techniques to our land, and unlike the $buddhist_ADJ$ sects of old, they have no previous ties to corrupt landowners or rebellious cities. We should welcome these foreigners into our cities, and see what benefits they could bring to our court.

name: Early Westernization
description: Thanks to frequent early contact with Western countries, we have learned a lot about foreign technology and other innovations. Using this knowledge, we can carry out reforms in economy, industry, and education that will help gain an edge over other clans.

name: Slave Raiding Wars
description: Slaves are the cornerstone of our economy. Attacking and raiding our neighbors to capture their population and enslave them is therefore the lifeblood of our country.

name: Nomadic Tendencies
description: Many of our people have lived their lives as nomads, as our custom has been to travel from one habitable place to the next. Even now, as everything changes and we build a city for our people, some retain their nomadic traditions, and continue to wander.

name: Land of the Ancestors
description: Land is not property, nor is it mere dust; it is our connection to our great forebears. From the better lands beyond, they watch over us. We must never let the connection between us be severed, and we must care for these lands in honor of those who first settled them.

name: Wandering Scholars
description: Communities of learned scholars of many faiths live in our lands, offering religious instruction to all who will listen.

name: Domain of Many Tongues
description: Our Empire is home to people from hundreds of different backgrounds. They speak a multitude of tongues, and come from all the directions of the horizon, but each in their own tongue pays homage to our ruler, binding us together.

name: Bound by Service
description: We are one people, and we have one army. By bringing troops from across all of our territories together, and pressing conquered peoples into military service, we can better integrate them into our society, and also increase their acceptance of our rule.

name: Regnal Chronicles
description: We should record the history of our splendid rulers and their illustrious deeds in great chronicles, so that they may be passed down across the generations and always remembered.

name: Control the Slave Trade
description: The demand for $slaves_goods$ from external traders grows greater by the day. Our position in $africa$ makes us the ideal middlemen for this trade. Let us encourage those that seek slave markets to do so in our lands, and to make their business in our marketplaces.

name: Gifts and Hostages
description: While our people are now united, the act of bending the knee to a common overlord has not come easy to them. By summoning all subjugated rulers to the capital, we can employ them as prestigious royal envoys. Some would call this a policy of hostage-taking; we simply see it as a way to remind our more independent-minded subjects of their loyalties.

name: People of Ornamentation
description: Our artisans are renowned far and wide, and it is said that they cannot leave a surface undecorated. Let us make the most of this reputation, and promote their creations as much as possible.

name: Courtly Competition
description: A preoccupied noble is a well-behaved noble. There are so many courtly titles in our realms that some say half of our men have one. Let us make sure our courtiers spend their time competing with one another for attention and visibility; they will be too busy to plot against our rule.

name: An Army Overnight
description: Our capital and other cities are built using army camps as a model. They have wings, vanguards, and fronts. In ensuring that military thinking permeates daily life, we will improve our overall combat readiness.

name: Mining Tradition
description: Our land is rich in rare materials, ready to be ripped from the earth and sold to foreign merchants for large profits. We would be foolish not to exploit this.

name: Far-Reaching Trade
description: Our merchants frequently bring back fascinating things from the courts of faraway countries. Perhaps it would be possible to reach even further shores?

name: Expanded Grazing Grounds
description: Our territory has plenty of land which is well-suited for grazing animal herds, making it easy for us to expand our output of $livestock$.

name: Sturdy Grains Agriculture
description: A stronger focus on agricultural production will help our people thrive. Thankfully, we have the ample space and fertile soil necessary to grow a number of crops.

name: $hand_cannon_guild$
description: Primitive metal tubes which were a lesser form of later, more advanced guns. First developed in $CHI$, the early hand cannon spread to $KOR$ and $JAP$ in 1270.

name: Sāqiyah
description: The $saquiyah$ is a mechanical device designed to ease the transportation of water to higher elevations. Also known as the #italic Persian wheel#!, #italic tablia#!, #italic rehat#!, and #italic tympanum#!, the wheel is crucial in the irrigation systems in areas with little to no flowing water.

name: Riches of $asia$
description: $asia$ is famous around the world for its riches. From the bountiful cities of $persia_region$ and $india$, to the highly-sought luxury items produced in $china$, to the almost mythical Spice Islands in $indonesia_region$, the luxurious goods coming from $asia$ are highly prized worldwide.

name: Silk Road
description: Be it the land route crossing the Gobi Desert and $persia_region$, or its ocean counterpart through the $indian_ocean_region$ and $indonesia_region$, the lands of $asia$ have been for centuries traversed by merchants seeking profit on the famous Silk Road.

name: Exchange of Ideas
description: Not only do coin and profit move along the $silk_road$, but ideas and knowledge also follow the ebb and flow of the merchants traveling along its path.

name: Legacy of Great Empires
description: From the Dragon Throne of $china$, to the various empires of $persia_region$, to the powerful $hindu_ADJ$ and $buddhist_ADJ$ dynasties of $india$ and $south_east_asia$, $asia$ has been home to many mighty empires throughout history.

name: Arduous Terrain
description: $asia$ is home to some very inhospitable lands, from the high peaks of the Himalaya, to the arid span of the Gobi Desert, to the dense jungles of $india$ and $south_east_asia$. And that does not even include the monsoon and typhoon seasons, and the almost constant present of earthquakes! Its people have learned to live in such an unwelcoming environment, but invaders will not find it so easy.

name: Fertile Lands
description: In general, the lands of $asia$ are blessed with plentiful rain, and many rivers cross its territories even in areas with less precipitation. Except for some of the most arid areas of the desert, our land provides ample food to our population. Even in those regions where it does not, the people living there are able to do much with what they have.

name: Crossroads of Religions
description: $hindu$, $buddhist$, $muslim$, and even $tengri$ are religions that have expanded into parts of the world very far from their places of origin. $asia$ has witnessed this exchange of beliefs for centuries, and in many cases the blending and syncretism that has happened among them.

name: Religious Syncretism
description: Interaction between beliefs sometimes results in synthesis rather than rejection. Foreign thoughts and practices should therefore not be seen as hostile threats, but opportunities to learn, and possibly incorporate valuable elements into our own traditions.

name: Source of Knowledge
description: While foreign nations pride themselves on being at the forefront of knowledge and development, some of their recent 'inventions' have been known in $asia$ for centuries. From the technological prowess of $china$ to the ancient literature of $india$, there is nothing for the East to envy from the West.

name: Structured Society
description: Religious and philosophical traditions, particularly those of $hindu$ and $SECT_CONFUCIANISM_NAME$, have historically influenced social organization in parts of $asia$, emphasizing proscribed role fulfillments within social hierarchies. The rigidity of living within these systems is offset by the relative ease with which social order is maintained.

name: $incense$ Preeminence
description: $incense$ has been a staple of life in $asia$ for centuries, maybe more so than anywhere in the world. Although other religions also use it for their rituals, its near-ubiquity in $hindu_ADJ$ and $buddhist_ADJ$ ceremonies, as well as its everyday use by $muslim$ people, give it a constant presence anywhere in $asia$.

name: $incense$ Trade Route
description: The high demand for $incense$, not only in $asia$ but also beyond it, requires the establishment of many trade routes dedicated to its commerce. Akin to the more famous $silk_road$, this trade of $incense$ links the East with the West.

name: Wake of the $MGE_ADJ$ Horde
description: There is almost no place in $asia$ that has not felt the influence of the $MGE_ADJ$ conquests. After the fall of the once-great empire forged by $genghis_khan_name_no_tooltip$, the land is finally recovering from being trampled by his horses.

name: Cultural Melting Pot
description: $asia$ is a highly diverse region, home to a wide variety of cultures. This diversity, and the cultural exchange and blended influences that result from it, has empowered our countries and allowed them to flourish in every domain from architecture to music to horticulture, and beyond.

name: Rise of Great Individuals
description: History proves that the most extraordinary individuals are the ones who rise to prominence and achieve great things. Time and again, empires have been forged or destroyed by the hand of a single ruler, and such achievements are to be respected and admired.

name: Sepak Takraw
description: Having been practiced all over $south_east_asia$ for a long time since its adaptation from the ancient $chinese_group$ #italic Cùjū#!, and also known as #italic Sepak Raga#!, #italic Takraw#!, #italic Chinlone#!, or #italic Sipa#! depending on the country, #italic $sepak_takraw$#! is not just a game. Although the objective is to kick a ball between players and keep it in the air, it is also a way to have regular physical exercise, and thus played not only for entertainment but as military training for the army.

name: Three Teachings
description: The $three_teachings$ are a philosophy originating from $CHI$ which combines the teachings of $SECT_CONFUCIANISM_NAME$, $SECT_DAOISM_NAME$ and $buddhist$ into a harmonious, singular teaching. $SECT_CONFUCIANISM_NAME$ represents the ideology of the law while $SECT_DAOISM_NAME$ is the worldview of the radical intellectuals. These two opposite ends of the philosophical spectrum would then be connected with the philosophies of $buddhist$.

name: $n_baghlah$
description: $n_baghlah_desc$

name: Expansionist Ambitions
description: As the Balkans fractured, many rising powers looked outward. Ambitious rulers pursued integration of diverse lands under a single, stronger crown, taking advantage of $BYZ_ADJ$ weakness.

name: Poklisars
description: Since the earliest days of our nation, we have often cast our gaze beyond our borders, be it to establish profitable trade routes, placate formidable neighbors and build alliances, or even to forge robust partnerships against common adversaries. #italic Poklisars#! are the ambassadors who carry out these missions in our name.

name: Hajduks
description: As the central authority of medieval kingdoms fractures under the weight of imperial expansion, the social vacuum is filled by the Hajduks. Originally simple cattle drovers (#italic hajtó#!) and seasonal laborers, these men have transitioned into a semi-mythical class of guerrilla fighters and highwaymen. They operate in small, disciplined bands (#italic cheta#!) led by a #italic Harambaša#!, governed by strict internal codes of conduct that emphasize loyalty and the protection of the local peasantry (the #italic raja#!). In our eyes, they are nothing more than brigands; to the commoners, they are the only shield against the depredations of foreign tax collectors and unruly invaders. By codifying their presence within our military structure, we empower a force that thrives on the very lawlessness of the frontier.

name: Pandurs
description: The state must harness the ferocity of the frontier without succumbing to its chaos. The $cro_pandurs_recruitment$ — once mere night watchmen and local security — are reorganized by charismatic leaders into a professionalized light infantry. These soldiers are a terrifying sight on the European battlefield, accompanied by their own bands of martial music. They are the masters of skirmishes, specializing in raiding supply lines, screening the main army, and psychological warfare. While their discipline remains erratic and their propensity for plunder high, they provide a ruler with a flexible tool of intimidation that conventional line infantry cannot match.

name: Eastern African Trade
description: The lands of $east_africa$ are at the crossroads of great trade routes. From the land of $egypt_region$ and the ports of the Mediterranean through the $red_sea_area$, to the riches of the East accross the $indian_ocean_region$, and southwards along the $swahili_coast_region$, the bustling movement of goods and people is constant. The countries in these lands are thus also accustomed to exchanging goods and valuables as a means of establishing diplomatic relationships.

name: Ukrainian Farmlands
description: Ukraine, or the 'borderlands' in $slavic$ language, is one of the most fertile regions in $europe$. The lands along both banks of the great rivers are renowned for their rich black soil, yielding abundant harvests of grain, legumes, and fiber crops. Whoever holds these territories commands a significant agricultural advantage, supplying their realm's granaries and the markets of $europe$.

name: Tercios
description: #italic Tercio#! infantry were developed principally by the brilliant general Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba, called #italic El Gran Capitán#!, during the Italian Wars. It is a mixed infantry formation of pikemen and musketeers. Because of this combined-arms approach, the formation simultaneously utilizes both the rigidity of its heavy infantry and the long-range firepower of its musketeers, making it an ideal defensive and offensive formation.

name: $CAT_ADJ$ Galleys
description: The $n_catalan_galley$ is a larger version of the ancient Greek galleys that once dominated the Mediterranean Sea.

name: Early $iberia_region_ADJ$ Caravels
description: Originally of $iberia_region_ADJ$ origin, the first caravels were small but very fast ships that were used for offshore fishing and coastal trade. Their use in $iberia$ is so widespread that the region can easily boast of possessing the most advanced caravels.

name: $iberia_region_ADJ$ Caravels
description: The need for faster and more reliable caravels has driven our shipbuilding experts to make improvements to their design. While caravels have become common across $europe$, the $iberia_region_ADJ$ models remain superior in both innovation and speed.

name: Early $iberia_region_ADJ$ Galleons
description: An early, but powerful ocean-going vessel, the $n_early_iberian_galleon$ is an original invention from $iberia$ that has a lower forecastle and a long hull, making them especially stable and resistant to headwinds.

name: Square-Rigged Caravels
description: By combining the $n_iberian_caravel$ and the $n_carrack$, a new ship has been born: fast, strong, and exactly what we need help us dominate the seas.

name: $iberia_region_ADJ$ Galleons
description: The $n_iberian_galleon$ is a more stylized version of the $n_early_iberian_galleon$. They are tremendously powerful vessels that absolutely crush any opposition on the high seas.

name: $a_almogavars$
description: $a_almogavars_desc$

name: $a_catalan_crossbowmen$
description: $a_catalan_crossbowmen_desc$

name: $a_late_almogavars$
description: $a_late_almogavars_desc$

name: $a_lanzas_de_castilla$
description: $a_lanzas_de_castilla_desc$

name: Caçadores
description: Nicknamed the #italic Fighting Cocks#!, the #italic Caçadores#! are an elite light infantry unit in the $POR_ADJ$ Army who wear brown uniforms to distinguish them from regular soldiers.

name: Indonesian Archipelago
description: Maritime connections naturally play a huge role within our society, as we are surrounded by waters. Our reliance on maritime trade and transport makes traversal of the seas a trivial task for our people.

name: Naval Prowess
description: Our political relevance within the archipelago almost solely relies on the strength of our naval forces. By improving our shipwrighting techniques and crew training, we will ensure our domination over the lesser states of $indonesia_region$.

name: Trade Hub of the East
description: No matter their origin or destination, every trader in $asia$ will eventually have to cross our lands, bringing both precious goods and tales of their travels with them.

name: Land of Many People
description: Our islands are home to many different people, speaking different languages and believing in many different gods. Only if we establish a common understanding and tolerance between them can we secure a prosperous country.

name: Great Families of $ITA$
description: After the foundation of our unified $ITA_ADJ$ state, we have absorbed many great noble families into our country. We should utilize their prestige and reputation to improve our own, while keeping those capable people busy.

name: Great Condottieri Captains
description: Our nation is renowned for producing great military minds, whether they serve their own interests or are sworn in loyalty to the state. We should ensure that these adept intellects are willing to serve us first and foremost.

name: $a_genoese_crossbowmen$
description: $a_genoese_crossbowmen_desc$

name: $n_genoese_galley$
description: $n_genoese_galley_desc$

name: Three Sisters Agriculture
description: Our land is plentiful, with many crops, but the method of cultivating maize, beans, and squash together is one of our greatest agricultural achievements. Grown together, these crops have a better output than they do when planted separately.

name: Mound Builders
description: The ceremonial mounds built by our ancestors are monuments to their sophisticated earthwork engineering skills. By incorporating these mounds into the planning of our infrastructure, we will preserve a defining tradition of our civilization.

name: Medicinal Infusions
description: The healing properties of certain plants have helped our people overcome different diseases for centuries. Infusions of certain leaves have even been said to lengthen the lives of our people.

name: Canoes
description: Lightweight canoes are perfectly adapted to the waterways of $north_america$. These vessels can navigate shallow rivers and are light enough to portage — carry overland— when necessary. In this way, we can turn disconnected waterways into full trade routes, making it much easier to direct the flow of commerce and people.

name: Seasonal Economy
description: In troubled times, we must learn to endure life, and life is synonymous with nature. The change of seasons necessitates a change in our lifestyles; villages must be adaptable and mobile.

name: Fishing Habits
description: Sometimes it is difficult to believe that some of our people were born on land and not in the water, for their bodies swim with such agility that it is nearly impossible to distinguish them from the current of the river. As a result, we are experts at fishing.

name: Whale Hunters
description: Whales, porpoises, walruses, seals... everything the sea gives us, we hunt.

name: Maple Syrup
description: The many maple trees in our country produce great quantities of sap, which can be collected and boiled to create a delicious sweet syrup and other confections.

name: Stickball Game
description: The ancient tradition of playing the stickball game has been part of our culture for ages. Used for ritual purposes or to settle disputes, hundreds of warriors gather in a field with wooden sticks and a single ball, which must be directed towards a marked goal. This practice not only brings our people together, but keeps our warriors in prime condition.

name: Warrior Societies
description: Our people have long organized into warrior societies, brotherhoods bound by oaths, shared rituals, and a common duty to defend their kin. By formalizing these traditions into Warrior Lodges, we can train a new class of dedicated fighters whose skill and resolve will keep our communities strong long after European weapons arrive on our shores.

name: Bison Hunters
description: Bison are a crucial resource for our people. We use every part of the animal as a tribute to its sacrifice. We feed our people with its flesh, we use its bones for tools; we use its fur to protect ourselves against the cold and its hides for our clothes. Even the animal's soul has symbolic meaning for us. Such is the importance of the bison to our culture that we would feel lost without them.

name: Federation Builders
description: We should unite with other groups of our kin to form a federation, which will put mutual trust and development as its first priority.

name: Shared Knowledge
description: Innovation can come in many forms and if we want to stay ahead of rival tribes, we will need to explore every advantage we can get.

name: Slash and Burn Agriculture
description: An agricultural technique that involves strategically cutting and burning the vegetation to obtain a nutrient-rich layer of ash that fertilizes underlying soil, making it excellent land for planting crops. We have learned that the land becomes stronger after this method, as a bone becomes stronger after being broken.

name: Council of Elders
description: Our tribal government ensures that everyone in it has a voice and an equal say in crucial decisions. This collaborative administration encourages us to consider new perspectives.

name: $fur$ Trade
description: Trading $fur$ with other tribes and foreigners is an essential part of our economy. We take great pride in our hunting abilities, and therefore are able to provide the best quality pelts.

name: Wampum
description: A mix of white and purple beads made from different kinds of shells, wampum are used for many purposes, such as recording treaties and oral histories, facilitating diplomacy, and functioning as a system of exchange in trade. Wampum appears wherever our people tread.

name: Shared Brotherhood
description: United in the teachings of the Great Law of Peace, our people maintain a strong sense of brotherhood and unity, despite their disparate tribal background.

name: Tributary System
description: Direct rule comes at the cost of extensive investment in subjugating and pacifying rival groups. By instead installing a loyal official to rule locally and demanding they pay an annual tribute, we eliminate threats from any rival $altepetl$ while filling our treasury at the same time.

name: Pyramid Architecture
description: Our ancestors constructed massive stone pyramids in the far-gone days of Teōtīhuacān, Tik'al, Copan, and Palenque. We have not forgotten the art of pyramid building, and can carry on this tradition.

name: Tlachtli
description: The heart of social life in our society is the ball game, where players strive to keep the ball inside the playing court by striking it with their hips. It is both a ritual alternative to warfare and a large part of religious life.

name: War Bonfires
description: A network of frontier settlements linked together by immense bonfires, which can be seen from a huge distance when lit, will allow us to quickly alert multiple settlements at once to threats, and therefore respond far faster.

name: Merchant-Officials
description: Merchants and their trading contribute substantially to our national income. However, merchants are also excellent sources of information, as they are often in the position to observe first-hand what circumstances our neighbors are in. By giving them official roles in the government, we can exploit their knowledge and mobility to our own ends.

name: Copperworking
description: Our artisans have begun to craft tools out of $copper$, a precious metal found throughout our territory. If we were to master this art, it would give us a tremendous advantage over our neighbors.

name: Obsidian Weaponry
description: Obsidian is an excellent material for making all kinds of tools and weapons. The hard, glasslike rock holds a sharp edge beautifully, making it an easy task to create blades, spearheads, or arrowheads which leave deadly wounds on any foe.

name: Precious Stone Carving
description: Our area is rich in precious stones, which are excellent for adding color, detail, and sparkle to artistic pieces and mundanities alike. Our craftsmen will immortalize themselves through these glittering jewels, and create great monuments to our culture.

name: Cultivate the Land
description: The jungle is a harsh environment in which to live, especially for farming cultures. Clearing portions of the jungle to create arable land is therefore one of our most vital tasks. We must organize our people in such a way that we can employ large labor forces to carry out these works whenever the need arises.

name: The Feathered Serpent
description: The legend of the Feathered Serpent is well-known across our lands. Although this figure represents many things to many people, such as Quetzalcōātl among the $nahua_group$, K'uk'ulkan among the $maya_language$ or Q'uq'umatz among the $kiche_culture$, he is a unifying figure for all of them.

name: Ritual Bloodletting
description: Many cultures in this region consider ritual sacrifice and bloodletting by the ruler as a way of paying homage to the gods. Maintaining this tradition pleases the gods and affirms our right to rule through divine tribute.

name: Inter-Valley Irrigation
description: By building extensive networks of canals and connecting the waterways of our homeland's valleys, we can greatly improve our irrigation techniques and the productivity of our farmlands.

name: Relocating Artisans
description: It is not fitting that territories we have conquered should have better artisans and wiser advisors than in our capital. The greatest hands and minds of the empire must be brought to the capital to serve us directly.

name: Terrace Farming
description: To take maximum advantage of the limited space in our highlands, we have developed terrace farming, a series of step-like platform fields on the sides of the mountains, as well as better irrigation techniques.

name: Summit Fortresses
description: Our cities and fortresses occupy the tops of immense mountains, well past the clouds. They present a formidable obstacle to anyone who might attempt to invade us.

name: River Trade
description: The bounty of our great rivers and seas has always fed our people. Let us embrace the river trade, and do what we can to protect the many merchants that travel along the coast to the mouth of the mighty river, so that we may never lack for the fine goods they bring us.

name: Rainforests and Mountaintops
description: The rainforests and mountains of our land are teeming with life. Apart from the spirits of the forests, jaguars, anacondas, tarantulas, and a myriad of other animals live among us, and for someone who knows them, they offer little direct danger. To an invading enemy, however, these lands might seem like a fortress and the wild animals as its defenders.

name: Talking Knots
description: By using arrangements of cords and knots to record information, we can greatly facilitate administration of our lands and keeping accurate records of vital information.

name: Llama Rearing
description: Our vast herds of llamas provide us with fabrics to clothe ourselves, meat to feed ourselves, and pack animals to carry our burdens. They are truly invaluable.

name: Mountain Roads Network
description: To facilitate easier distribution of goods, a great network of mountain roads connecting far-off valleys together and crossing deep gorges is required. Let us build it.

name: Tears of the Sun
description: Though adventurers from far-off lands dream of finding secret gold on mountain trails high in the Andes, to us the yellow metal has more artistic and sacred importance than simple economic value.

name: Hidden Cities
description: In a land of immense peaks and impenetrable rainforests, many of our cities are nearly inaccessible to outsiders. They could easily remain hidden for centuries, forgotten by the world.

name: Potato Production
description: Since maize grows poorly in the high plateaus of our land, we have learned to rely instead on the highly nutritious roots of a local plant. With increased production, we can feed our people and our warriors with this easily maintained crop.

name: Head Hunters
description: Conquering territory from weaker peoples is a necessary evil in our state. These circumstances have created a unique warrior code, according to which capturing and not killing the enemy is the highest display of bravery and valor. This has made our warriors famous for their mastery in capturing people alive.

name: Skilled Raiders
description: Our raiders are famous for their ability to carry out lightning-fast attacks against unaware enemies. Their speed and ability to evade enemy retaliation should be studied and employed by our regular troops as well.

name: The $sahel_region$ Trade
description: Caravans have been trading between the $sahel_region$ and the Mediterranean for ages, the benefits from this trade greatly outweighing the perils of crossing the burning sands of the Sahara.

name: Cavalry Raids
description: From the time of our ancestors, horsemen have been the agents of our conquests. The thunder of their hooves ringing across the grasslands of the $sahel_region$ spread fear in our enemies, and have brought us many victories.

name: Four Noble Truths
description: The foundational teachings of the Buddha, the $four_noble_truths$ explain the reality of being. Nothing is permanent, which causes pain to the spirit, due to its attachment to this transient existence. This spiritual pain can only be eased by liberating oneself from desire and letting go of these attachments, which is achieved by following the $noble_eightfold_path$.

name: Noble Eightfold Path
description: The path to being liberated from Saṃsāra and achieving Nirvāṇa, the $noble_eightfold_path$ is the purest distillation of $buddhist_ADJ$ practices. Dictating both one's mental state and physical actions, it determines proper comportment for any follower of $buddhist$.

name: Middle Way
description: The Buddha teaches us that we should avoid extremes, as neither with sensual indulgence nor extreme asceticism can one achieve enlightenment.

name: Three Jewels
description: The $three_jewels$, or Three Refuges, are the three supports in which a follower of $buddhist$ takes refuge. These refuges are the #italic Buddha#!, the enlightened one; the #italic Dharma#!, the teachings of the Buddha; and the #italic Saṃgha#!, the monastic community that preserves the Dharma.

name: $buddhist_ADJ$ Syncretism
description: $buddhist$ has its origins in $india$, but it has since spread far and wide, coming in contact with many different beliefs. As such, it contains much syncretism not only with the previous $hindu_ADJ$ traditions, but with the many other deities it has been exposed to.

name: Sūtra
description: A type of sacred text in both $dharmic_ADJ$ and $buddhist_ADJ$ religions, they vary in format and content. Regardless, they are always considered to be valid sources of knowledge, and proper study of them is required if one is to develop their spirit.

name: $buddhist_ADJ$ Councils
description: Throughout $buddhist_ADJ$ history, monastic councils have discussed canonical texts across different schools. Although the specific form, outcomes, and records of the councils may vary from school to school, the unifying power of such councils — bringing diverse traditions into dialogue — should not be underestimated.

name: $buddhist_ADJ$ Canon
description: Called different names and even containing different texts, depending on the branch of $buddhist$, the $buddhist_canon$ is a collection of sacred $buddhist_ADJ$ texts. Containing everything from monastic rules to #italic Sūtra#!, or teachings of the Buddha, any person dedicated to $buddhist$ should be familiar with them.

name: $pali_language$ Canon
description: Although there are many different canons in $buddhist$, depending on the school, the $theravada_ADJ$ $pali_canon$ is the oldest and most prestigious. Other schools have created their canons from a mix of texts with various sources, but the $pali_canon$ has remained unchanged since the times of Ashoka 'the Great', and contains the words of the Buddha himself. It has also served as the foundation of many other schools.

name: $buddhist_ADJ$ Universities
description: Since antiquity, $buddhist_ADJ$ centers have also been hubs of learning and knowledge, attracting people from all over to study in our institutions. Nālandā was the biggest of these centers in the past, but many others have followed in its footsteps since.

name: Xuánzàng Travels
description: Xuánzàng, a $chinese_group$ $buddhist_ADJ$ monk who lived during the Táng dynasty in the 7th century, embarked on a seventeen-year overland trip to $india$ in order to visit it centers of learning and to gather a great number of $buddhist$ texts. Among other places he visited Nālandā, where he learned from the best masters, and on his return to $china$ he brought with him more than a thousand documents, which made a great contribution to $mahayana$. His trip and his records served as basis for the tale of #italic Journey to the West#!, in which a monk is tasked by the Buddha to travel to $india$ in search of some holy texts. accompanied among others by the Monkey King, Sūn Wùkōng.

name: Silk Road Transmission
description: It is undeniable the effect that the Silk Road has had on the spread of $buddhist$. Whether via land or sea, trade has allowed $buddhist$ to spread far from its origins in $india$.

name: Bodhisattva
description: Regardless of the school of $buddhist$ one adheres to, a $bodhisattva$ is an important figure, although their exact characteristics and importance vary between the different traditions. In all cases, however, they are deserving of reverence and admiration.

name: Avalokiteśvara
description: Also known as Guānyīn or Kannon, $avalokitesvara$ is one of the most revered Bodhisattvas. Represented as a male or female depending on the school, and even in some considered to be the origin of all $hindu_ADJ$ deities, $avalokitesvara$ is the $bodhisattva$ of compassion, and is associated with the mantra #italic Oṃ maṇi padme hūm̐#!.

name: Maitreya
description: $maitreya$ is currently a $bodhisattva$, prophesized to be the future and final Buddha of the current era. His destiny is to reestablish the teachings of the Dharma in the world after they have been forgotten by humanity, and as such he is the successor of Siddhārtha Gautama.

name: Mount Meru
description: $mount_meru$ is the sacred mountain at the center of the universe in both the physical and spiritual sense for $hindu$, $buddhist$, and $jain$. As it is the center around which everything else revolves, so does our entire country revolve around our ruler.

name: Naraka
description: Also called #italic Niraya#!, $naraka$ refers to the realms of suffering where one's bad karma is cleansed before being reincarnated. There are many $naraka$ realms, and both the time an individual must reside in them and the punishments they will receive while doing so depends on how much karma they need to gain before being reborn in one of the upper realms.

name: Four Heavenly Kings
description: Each presiding over one of the cardinal directions, the $four_heavenly_kings$ are in charge of protecting the Deva realm from the Asuras. They are also responsible for assessing the virtue and morality of mortals.

name: Vegetarianism
description: Although it depends on the school, there are some rules in the Dharma regarding abstinence from meat consumption. Each school has different views about the strictness of this abstinence, and also whether it should apply only to the monastic community or to the population in general.

name: Edicts of Ashoka
description: A legal code published by Emperor Ashoka 'the Great' in the 3rd century BCE, these edicts include strictures promoting for $buddhist$. Although this code is from many centuries ago, it still deserves respect and reverence from any member of the $buddhist_ADJ$ faithful.

name: Five Precepts
description: The foundational code of $buddhist_ADJ$ ethics and morality, the $five_precepts$ represent the most basic rules believers must follow in $buddhist$, whether part of the ordained monastic community or not. They instruct people to abstain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxication.

name: Monastic Communities
description: $buddhist_ADJ$ life is centered around its communities of monks and nuns, called the #italic Saṃgha#!. They are governed by the #italic Vinaya#!, the rules and precepts that dictate the operations of any $buddhist_ADJ$ religious community.

name: Prestigious Schools
description: $buddhist$ has developed into a myriad of schools, each one centered around one type of monastic community and declaring a preference for certain texts. However, some of these schools have gained recognition, while others have been relegated to obscurity. Associating with the more prestigious schools gives those people a bit of prestige as well.

name: Offerings
description: It is a precept of $buddhist$ to make offerings to the $three_jewels$ in order to accumulate merit. These offerings may be material or non-material, and some monastic communities depend completely on food donated by their followers for their survival.

name: Incense Burning
description: The practice of burning incense is a staple of any $buddhist_ADJ$ ritual or offering. Varying in shapes and forms, it is common for both lay people and ordained monks and nuns alike to light incense before performing any ritual or meditation. As such, the smell of incense constantly permeates any $buddhist_ADJ$ temple.

name: Ascetic Practices
description: Although the Buddha warned us about the dangers of extreme asceticism, some among the monastic community still perform these strict practices. Limiting the type of cloth they can wear, the food they can eat, or where they can live are some of the restrictions adopted by those who wish to walk this path. Although such abstemious behavior is not a requirement for obtaining merit, it has its own benefits for the practitioner.

name: Mindfulness
description: An essential part of $buddhist_ADJ$ practice, $mindfulness$ means to be aware of the phenomena of both body and mind, while keeping the teachings of the Buddha always present in the mind. With this, one can avoid the arising of unwanted states, and develop into the wanted ones.

name: Dāna
description: Denoting generosity, $dana$ is defined as the act of giving without anything in return, and is a key virtue in all religions related to the Dharma. Helping others selflessly, whereas individually or communally, is one of the key ways of accumulating karma.

name: Ahiṃsā
description: The concept of $ahimsa$, or nonviolence, is a key virtue among all religions following the Dharma. Any conflict is encouraged to be resolved peacefully through dialogue, rather than the use of force. Unfortunately, that is not always possible, but violence should always be the last resort, and its use must be just.

name: Resistance to Persecution
description: Although it has spread widely throughout the world, $buddhist$ has also seen its fair share of persecution across the ages. Its temples and images may have been destroyed, its followers slaughtered or forced into hiding, but nonetheless its faithful have persevered.

name: $buddhist_ADJ$ Meditation
description: Meditation is a common practice among all $buddhist_ADJ$ followers, regardless of their school. The aim is to train the mind and the spirit to develop mindfulness, tranquility, and insight, and thus ultimately achieve enlightenment.

name: Universal $christian$
description: We must pursue good relations with our fellow $christian_ADJ$ faithful of all denomination, even if we consider some of their practices to be heresy.

name: Roman Orthodoxy
description: The righteousness of the Roman $catholic_ADJ$ faith and its doctrines must remain unquestioned, in order to entrench its authority in the minds of our people.

name: Devotion to the Virgin Mary
description: Our dedication to the Virgin Mary must remain a central pillar of our worship.

name: Baltic Crusades Experience
description: In this country, we have a long tradition of sending our finest knights and aristocrats to spread the true faith to heathens in the $baltic_region$ and Mediterranean regions. We will fulfill our $christian_ADJ$ mission by bringing the faith to the unenlightened, while also acquiring experienced commanders for our armies.

name: $catholic_ADJ$ Pilgrims
description: The holy sites of our faith should be seen by every follower. Encouraging pilgrimages, and elevating those who have undergone the process, should be a priority of our administration.

name: Inquisition
description: The Inquisition was created in the 12th century as a means to combat the Cathar heresy, but its reach grew significantly in the Late Middle Ages as the main tool of the $catholic_ADJ$ Church to counter the spread of dissident doctrines.

name: Itinerant Preaching Friars
description: Preaching friars — members of $mendicant_orders$ like the Dominicans and Franciscans — have taken their ministry beyond the monastery walls to preach directly among the people. By supporting and praising them openly for these acts of devotion, we can strengthen religious conviction throughout the realm, even among the most remote peasants.

name: Devotio Moderna
description: The #italic Devotio Moderna#!, or modern devotional movement, is rapidly gaining popularity among members of our faith. We should implement some of their teachings into our court, so as to make ourselves appear particularly devout.

name: Denunciation of Heretics
description: We must ensure the supremacy of the one true faith, and denounce all criticisms of it as the bitterest of heresy.

name: Lay Religious Orders
description: Many of the faithful have devoted themselves to a life of prayer and good works, which usually comes with taking the veil or becoming a monk. However, they have not taken formal vows, and act without official $PAP_ADJ$ approval. Nevertheless, we should support these popular efforts to do good deeds and help our people.

name: Conquistadors
description: The discovery of the New World attracts adventurers of all stripes to risk their fortunes and lives on uncertain expeditions, with the promise of unparalleled wealth, fame, and power. These expeditions are formalized through agreements between expedition leaders and the government, legally manifested as 'capitulations of conquest'.

name: Grand Displays of Faith
description: To honor God, we need to construct great monuments in His name. Not only will this display our devotion to our faith, but it will also demonstrate the magnificent skills of our sculptors and architects.

name: Monastic Frugality
description: The holy occupants of our monasteries are bastions of sensible, frugal living. Our clergy should consider adapting their own lifestyles to more closely resemble those of these monks and nuns.

name: Reformed Church Music
description: We must accept the proposed reforms to our liturgical music. The diluted, soulless tunes currently in fashion can no longer be considered acceptable ways to express the glory of the divine.

name: Frequent Councils
description: It has been proposed that holding religious councils more frequently would prevent theological disputes and criticisms from festering unchecked. While we may not have full control over the curia, we can at least use our influence to encourage regular synods that address relevant issues before they can become crises.

name: Mendicant Orders
description: The orders of our faith, who have taken vows of poverty and live itinerant lives, have brought assistance to many remote parts of our country. We should support their efforts as much as we can without disrupting their holy missions.

name: Exsurge Domine
description: To eradicate the evil of heresy, the Lord Himself will arise and purge them from our lands!

name: Refute False Confessions
description: In these turbulent times, we must clearly define orthodox $christian_ADJ$ doctrine, while systematically refuting the false beliefs that endanger the very souls of our people.

name: Roman Catechism
description: Our clergy must adopt the official Roman Catechism as their guide for instruction. This text will improve priestly education and ensure only consistent, orthodox teachings are transmitted to the populace.

name: Overseas Missions
description: Our clergy is ready and willing to spread our faith into new territories overseas. With their contribution, settling new lands will be made easier and cheaper.

name: Baptism Records
description: We must confirm baptism as an important cornerstone of our faith by keeping meticulous records of who in our population has or has not yet been baptized.

name: Second $scholasticism$
description: We will need to revive and refine the philosophical movement of medieval scholasticism.

name: $sunday_schools_advance$
description: $sunday_schools_advance_desc$

name: Index of Forbidden Books
description: The dangerous ideas of the Reformation will spread like a toxic fungus in the minds of our subjects if they have access to written works propagating these silly thoughts! We must forbid certain dangerous texts, and keep a comprehensive list of which books are not allowed.

name: Cuius Regio, Eius Religio
description: #italic Whose realm, his religion.#! We will have to accept that other countries follow other faiths, and that this will sometimes be a crucial factor in diplomacy.

name: Promote Baroque Art
description: Our faith has a long tradition of sponsoring and promoting great works of art. The development of the splendid new Baroque style reflects the pathos and glory of our theology beautifully, and should receive particular sponsorship.

name: National Church
description: The State must take greater control over the Church in our land. We cannot allow foreign entities to exercise undue influence over our ecclesiastical administration; our Church must serve our realm first.

name: Entrenched Church
description: No matter which people we rule over, the Church provides a way to give them a unified structure.

name: $catholic_ADJ$ Enlightenment
description: For our faith to withstand the attacks of the Enlightenment, we must adapt, and present new perspectives in and about the Church.

name: Divine Church Music
description: Many of our composers have created their greatest works thanks to the inspiration provided by their faith. We should actively seek out the most talented artists and hire them immediately so as to never let our churches and cathedrals suffer from inferior music.

name: Missionary Works
description: Missionary efforts to carry our faith to the far corners of the world can never be considered finished. We need to sponsor more missions to further bring the light of $catholic$ to these unilluminated souls.

name: Epic Poetry
description: For millennia our people have preserved the legends of gods and heroes through epic poetry. Works such as Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, alongside Hesiod's Theogony, stand among the greatest monuments of our cultural heritage. These timeless narratives continue to shape our identity and inspire generations.

name: Tales of the Blessed Isles
description: The Makaron Nesoi, the Blessed Isles, are believed to be the ultimate destination of the most virtuous souls. Those who live lives of piety and excellence may earn their place among heroic spirits in the Elysian fields. Tales of these sacred realms inspire the pursuit of virtue, honor, and moral excellence throughout society.

name: Religious Dialects
description: Although our faith is shared across many communities, notable divergence exists in ritual, tradition, and local religious practice. Over time these variations develop organically, sometimes even within the same province. Much like language evolves into regional dialects, our religious customs gradually form distinct local expressions while remaining within the same sacred tradition.

name: Offerings to the Moirai
description: Each year a portion of our ritual offerings is dedicated to the three Moirai, the Fates who govern destiny itself. Clotho the Spinner, Lachesis the Alloter of life's portion, and Atropos the inevitable end preside over the completion of every mortal life according to the cosmic order. In many theological traditions their authority is considered primordial, sometimes even surpassing that of the gods.

name: On Hubris & Morality
description: The principles of our faith originate from the will of the gods and are interpreted through priests, seers, and acts of divination. Through prophecy and sacred interpretation mortals attempt to understand the divine order of the cosmos. Yet the surest path to moral virtue remains piety, reverence, and the careful avoidance of destructive hubris.

name: Variety in Divine Identity
description: Our pantheon contains a remarkable variety of deities, each representing different virtues, crafts, and ideals. This diversity allows every individual to discover a divine patron that resonates with their life and vocation. The modest altar of a blacksmith to Hephaestus carries meaning equal to the noble devotion offered to Zeus.

name: Mystery Cults
description: Hidden behind masks, symbols, and sacred ritual, influential initiates gather within secretive mystery cults. These organizations exercise considerable social and political influence, shaping events through ritual authority, wealth, and discreet alliances. Wise rulers maintain good relations with these mystai, lest their influence and intrigue turn against the state.

name: The Teachings of Theogony
description: Hesiod's Theogony recounts the origins and genealogy of the gods, revealing the birth of the divine order itself. Through its verses, symbols of authority such as the scepter and the voice of rule are presented as sacred responsibilities. The work reminds rulers that true authority must be exercised through wisdom, moderation, and reason.

name: Unify the Priestly Class
description: For much of our history the priesthood responsible for sacred lands and temple revenues has functioned in a decentralized manner. Yet recent developments in foreign religious institutions have introduced new ideas of organization and central authority. These influences now encourage the unification and coordination of our own priestly hierarchy.

name: Śruti
description: Meaning 'that which is heard', $sruti$ are the holiest and most ancient texts of $hindu$. They are considered to be a divine revelation and thus not attributed to human authorship, although some deny their divine origin while still accepting their authority.

name: Vēdaḥ
description: The main texts among the $sruti$ are the $vedah$, which are the oldest $sanskrit_language$ texts. Their authorship is attributed to Brahmā in the $mahabarata$, and they are the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the Atharvaveda.

name: Smṛti
description: Meaning 'that which is remembered', $smrti$ texts are inspired by or originated from the $vedah$, and thus are considered less authoritative than the $sruti$ due to being derived from them. However, unlike the $sruti$, the $smrti$ texts have attributed authorship and are transmitted through manuscripts.

name: Mahābhārata
description: One of the two major $smrti$ texts together with the $ramayana$, the $mahabarata$ is an epic of ancient $india$. It is the longest epic poem ever written, about ten times bigger than the $greek_language$ #italic Iliad#! and #italic Odyssey#! combined, and it narrates the story of a dynastic struggle for the throne of the ancient $indian_group$ kingdom of Kuru culminating in the Kurukshetra War, also called $mahabarata$ War. The story ends with the death of $krishna_avatar$ and the end of his dynasty.

name: Rāmāyaṇa
description: One of the two major $smrti$ texts together with the $mahabarata$, the $ramayana$ is an epic of ancient $india$. It narrates the life of $rama_avatar$, avatar of $vishnu_god$, as a prince of the kingdom of Kosala. It emphasizes the importance of virtue in all aspects of one's life.

name: Purāṇa
description: Considered part of the $smrti$, the $purana$ are texts with a variety of content. Cosmology, divine genealogies, astronomy, grammar, love stories... almost everything can be found within them. As such, even though they are not part of the $sruti$, their influence on $hindu_ADJ$ beliefs and society is strong, as they combine diverse local beliefs and traditions into the common narrative of the $vedah$.

name: Ātman
description: Referred to the true and eternal unchanging Self, it is the essence of each individual's consciousness. According to the $astika$ schools, this $atman$ is distinct from the mind and body, and it is also different from the Jivātman that persists across multiple lifetimes. In contrast, the $nastika$ schools interpret the concept differently, or reject it entirely.

name: Nāstika Schools
description: Some schools of thought in $hindu$ deviate from the mainstream, rejecting the authority of the $vedah$ and the existence of $atman$. These schools, like $jain$ and $buddhist$, are thus heterodox, although they still contain many of the shared core beliefs of $hindu$.

name: Āstika Schools
description: Called the orthodox schools of $hindu$, they accept the authority of the $vedah$ and the existence of $atman$. Although consisting of many different branches, this commonality of acceptance gives the $astika_schools$ a lot of common ground.

name: Diversity of Beliefs
description: The beliefs of the people of $india$ center around the concept of Dharma and the text of the $vedah$, but they are manifested in a myriad of forms and practices. Even the gods recognized and worshiped are not the same for everyone, but a common thread of concepts is present throughout.

name: Īśvara
description: Interpreted differently depending on the school or branch of $hindu$, $ishvara$ refers to the Supreme Being or God. Therefore, it can refer to $shiva_god$ for $shaivism$, to $vishnu_god$ for $vaishnavism$, or to any personal god of the individual.

name: Sanskritization
