description: $hindu$ has spread much farther than its origins in $india$, and many other cultures and countries have adopted $sanskrit_language$ concepts and titles to refer to their own identity. As such, the concepts of $hindu$ have seamlessly permeated and blended into foreign beliefs.

name: Bhakti Movement
description: Having emerged in the 6th century, this movement promotes love and devotion to one's personal god or towards an enlightened individual. It appeals to the lay population by speaking to them directly on their own terms. A highly influential movement, it is changing how religion and belief themselves are understood by our people.

name: Yoga
description: A prominent $hindu_ADJ$ school and philosophy, $yoga$ is a set of practices both physical and spiritual, with the purpose of controlling the mind and body. Performed for millennia, it has almost become synonymous with the path of enlightenment.

name: Diwali
description: Called the festival of light, $diwali$ is when we celebrate the triumph of the Dharma; the victory of good over evil and light over darkness. We will light candles and lanterns to symbolize this victory, and we will honor our ancestors.

name: Holi
description: Held at the beginning of spring to celebrate its arrival, $holi$ is the festival of colors and love. We commemorate agriculture and good harvests, and at the same time enjoy the myriad of colors that spring offers. It is also the time to have fun and resolve conflicts, removing one's emotional impurities.

name: Holy Rivers
description: Rivers and their veneration have always been an important part of $hindu$. From the Indus to the Ganges, there are many rivers considered holy, on the shores of which many rituals are held. Their waters are considered sacred, and they are a common site for purification rituals.

name: Advaita Vedānta
description: Rejecting the dualism between consciousness and matter, $advaita_vedanta$ claims that the $atman$, or the innermost self or consciousness, is one and the same as the supreme reality or consciousness of the universe, Brahman. In this sense, the physical material world is just an illusion hiding the ultimate reality of the Brahman.

name: $hindu_ADJ$-$muslim_ADJ$ Relations
description: There has been a lot of interaction in the past between $hindu$ and $muslim$, and there will continue to be so. Our peoples have learned to live peacefully together and there has even been some degree of syncretism between the two faiths.

name: $hindu_ADJ$ Unification
description: Despite the differences in beliefs and practices throughout $hindu$, there are more commonalities between us than differences. A common unified view of $hindu$ has started to emerge, and our people can gain a great sense of unity through it.

name: $hindu_ADJ$ Architecture
description: Regardless of the style of construction, be it a Śikhara, Vimāna, or Prāṅg, $hindu_ADJ$ temples are recognizable everywhere for their tall, decorated towers. A representation of $mount_meru$, more or less emphasized depending on the region, these spires serve both as a signal of faith and a demonstration of power.

name: Varṇa System
description: Since the times of the $vedah$, there has existed the concept of one's Dharma being classified as one of the four possibles: #italic Brāhmaṇa#!, scholars or priests; #italic Kṣatriya#!, rulers or warriors; #italic Vaiśya#!, farmers or merchants; or #italic Śūdra#!, artisans or servants. These classifications are not rigid, but instead represent the ideal of an individual's calling, and they have been very influential in $hindu_ADJ$ society.

name: Extreme Pacifism
description: Based on the concept of $ahimsa$, $hindu$ always advocates for pacifism and nonviolence. However, our enemies should still be wary of provoking us, lest we end up exemplifying the complete opposite extreme when roused into war.

name: $hindu_ADJ$ Empires
description: There have been many empires in the past that followed $hindu$. From the Maurya and Gupta empires in $india$, to the Śrīvijaya Empire in $indonesia_region$, and the long-lasting Chola Dynasty, $hindu$ has always been the spirital force behind the throne of powerful rulers.

name: Sacred Cattle
description: As part of $ahimsa$, it is prohibited to slaughter cattle. They instead are respected and venerated as maternal figures, and are symbols of selfless provision and sacrifice. Having been worshiped since the time of the $vedah$, they still command enormous respect and attention.

name: Second Council of Ephesus
description: The $second_council_of_ephesus$, convened in 449 at the instance of Pope Dioscorus of $alexandria$, was a legitimate $christian_ADJ$ council despite its denunciation by the $catholic_ADJ$ and $orthodox_ADJ$ Churches. At this council, the formula of Cyril of Alexandria — which states that Christ is a single incarnate nature, both human and divine — was officially accepted.

name: Rejection of Chalcedon
description: As they did not accept the $second_council_of_ephesus$, the Council of Chalcedon was called at the instance of Pope Leo I, who demanded the nullification of the $second_council_of_ephesus$. We reject this false council, and stand by the decisions made in the original one.

name: Monophysite vs $miaphysite_ADJ$
description: Although $miaphysite$ also proclaims that the figure of Christ has only a single nature, it differs substantially from the Eutychian Monophysite view which proclaims that the humanity of Christ was absorbed into his divinity. Though there may be some that also call us followers of Monophysitism, it is just an agreement in words, as in substance our views are clearly different.

name: Original $christian$
description: There have been many schisms and divisions in the $christian_ADJ$ world, but our creed traces its roots on the original true $christian$ formulated from the First Council of Nicaea. Every split from the main branch after this is mere heresy.

name: Beyond the Borders
description: $christian$ undoubtedly originated inside the cradle of the Roman Empire, and many of its branches have been content to stay in that region. $miaphysite$, however, was on the edges of the Empire after being denounced by the Chalcedonians, and has spread far beyond its birthplace, bringing the light of God to the most remote places.

name: Isolated Reaches
description: $miaphysite$ has managed to spread to very distant places. Even while surrounded by enemies and heretics, our faith has remained strong.

name: Independent Leaders
description: Due to the isolation of $miaphysite$, it has been difficult at times to contact other patriarchates. As such, our leaders have learned to act independently, while at the same time keeping in contact with the rest of the $christian_ADJ$ world as much as possible.

name: $jerusalem$ Focus
description: We always keep the holy city of $jerusalem$ in our minds, as not only it was the place where Jesus preached and died, but also where he will return to in his Second Coming. As such, we always pray facing in the direction of $jerusalem$, no matter where we are.

name: Acceptance of the Old Testament
description: Some $christian_ADJ$ denominations have decided to reduce the importance of the Old Testament, claiming that the arrival of Jesus completely supersedes it. We, however, maintain that it is still relevant, and that some instructions in it are as valid as they were when they were written.

name: Primacy of $alexandria$
description: Although $miaphysite$ has many branches and independent leaders, we recognize $alexandria$ and its seat as our spiritual leader. However, this is a sign of respect for the Apostolic Throne and a way to honor it, rather than a bestowal of any special prerogatives.

name: School of $alexandria$
description: The Catechetical $school_of_alexandria$, allegedly founded by the Apostle Mark himself, is the oldest school of catechism in the world. There, biblical and theological studies have been taught since the start of $christian$ itself. Although the school itself was destroyed when the Bishop of $rome$ was declared to be above the Patriarch of $alexandria$, its tradition has endured.

name: Preservation of Local Languages
description: Despite the importance of $greek_language$ and $latin_language$ in early $christian$, $miaphysite$ has preserved its liturgy in more local vernaculars, like $coptic_language$, $aramaic_language$, and $armenian_language$. Venerable languages in their own right, each $miaphysite_ADJ$ branch preserves its own historical tongue.

name: Double Patriarchate
description: Both $alexandria$ and $antioch$ see themselves as having two different patriarchates, one for $miaphysite$ and another for $orthodox$. Although they both may claim legitimacy, only $miaphysite$ preserves the true patriarchates.

name: Eastern $christian$
description: We are part of the branch of so-called $eastern_christianity$, which amalgamates many different denominations with different theological and liturgical traditions, but also with many common cultural aspects.

name: Life Among Heathens
description: The lands of the faithful have often been tainted by the presence of unbelievers, but this is why our clerics have ventured forth towards the unknown to bring the light of Jesus to distant lands. We have thus influenced these lost souls in more ways than what one might expect, even if we have not been able to make them see the error of their beliefs.

name: Gradual Departure
description: Although they were quick to brand us as heretics, $miaphysite$ did not cut ties with the rest of the $christian_ADJ$ world instantly. We kept in contact with the other patriarchates, and attended the councils, but it was gradually made clear that $miaphysite$ is too different from those heretical beliefs.

name: Thriving Under Persecution
description: Although our faithful have been persecuted by heretics for centuries, our beliefs have persevered. No matter how many times they bring us down, we will rise again!

name: Preserving National Identity
description: It is because of our history of being persecuted and oppressed that our Church became responsible for preserving our identity. It is in the bosom of the Church where our languages and traditions have been kept safe, and therefore we have unshakeable faith in this institution.

name: Defense Against Heretics
description: Ever since our split from other $christian_ADJ$ faiths, the heretics have come to us with accusations and condemnations many times. They may call themselves $christian_ADJ$, but their views are obviously clouded, whereas our vision is made clear by the light of God.

name: Remote Patriarchates
description: Conquest and persecution have repeatedly forced our patriarchates to relocate after their seats have fallen under control of heathen conquerors. Though we now operate from new locations, the original seats remain spiritually revered in our tradition, albeit from a distance.

name: Further Reaches
description: Despite many attempts by nonbelievers to stop our faith from spreading, it has nevertheless made its way to many different peoples and cultures, bringing light wherever it goes.

name: Internal Communion
description: Despite having independent patriarchs, all branches of $miaphysite$ maintain mutual communion. This helps them build relationships with each other, and promotes unity in the Church.

name: Cradle of Monasticism
description: Monasticism in $christian$ was born in $egypt_region$, when the $christian_ADJ$ faithful retreated to the desert to pray and dedicate their lives to God. $miaphysite$ can therefore claim this history as their own through the Alexandrine tradition.

name: Unique Architecture
description: The relative isolation of our patriarchates have resulted in the development of unique architectural styles for our holy places. Although other $christian_ADJ$ denominations may be more prominent, our captivating architecture is an inspiration to the faithful.

name: People of $muslim_god_name$
description: We are the followers of $muslim_god_name$, the only true God, and abide by His Word. All those who believe in Him are our brothers and sisters in His eyes.

name: Holy Revelation
description: The Word of $muslim_god_name$ was revealed to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him, and transcribed in the Holy $common_string_quran$. Through its verses, $muslim_god_name$'s will is passed to His faithful, and all $muslim_ADJ$ believers should be familiar with its passages.

name: Islamic Calligraphy
description: $muslim$ is not only a religion of peace, but of the arts. The calligraphy used to write the verses of the $common_string_quran$ and the names of the prophets often straddles the line between scripture and art.

name: Aṣ-Ṣalāh Farḍ
description: One of the Five Pillars of $muslim$, Aṣ-Ṣalāh is the obligation for a $muslim_ADJ$ faithful to perform daily prayers. Although the number of times one must pray every day and the specific movements when doing it may vary from school to school, the act of daily prayer is common among all $muslim$.

name: Al-Zakāh Wājib
description: One of the Five Pillars of $muslim$, Al-Zakāh is a form of almsgiving considered a religious obligation for any $muslim_ADJ$ faithful. Giving money to help the needy is a mandatory charity for everyone that can afford it, and it is considered a tax.

name: $muslim_ADJ$ Lineage
description: Ever since the times of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, $muslim$ has been intrinsically linked to rulership structures. As such, our dynastic line is also legitimized by the faith itself.

name: $muslim_ADJ$ Caravans
description: From the many paths of the Silk Road, to the salt routes across the Sahara, our people have a tradition of embarking on trade ventures to faraway lands, providing us and the rest of the $muslim_ADJ$ world with a wide selection of available goods.

name: Islamic Golden Age
description: The impact that the $islamic_golden_age$ had on the entire world, not only in $muslim_ADJ$ countries, is absolutely undeniable. Some of these infidel nations are only now emerging from their dark ages of ignorance, making their first attempts at artistic and scientific 'discoveries' that we invented — and perfected — long ago.

name: Ramaḍān
description: A commemoration of the first revelation to Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him, the month of $ramadan$ is the holiest month in $muslim$. During this month, all $muslim_ADJ$ faithful are expected to perform Ṣawm — fasting and abstinence — during the daylight hours, as well as prayer and reflection.

name: Sunnah
description: Consisting of the traditions and practices attributed to Muḥammad, peace be upon him, the $sunnah$ dictates how every $muslim_ADJ$ faithful should behave, and is also what gives $sunni$ its name. Although the different schools of jurisprudence may vary on the details, they all have their basis in the $sunnah$.

name: Imamate
description: The basis of $shia_ADJ$ faith is that Muḥammad, peace be upon him, designated 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib as his successor. As such, the figure of Imām is that of a spiritual leader coming from the line of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, to lead all $muslim_ADJ$ faithful.

name: Indian Sea Trade
description: $muslim_ADJ$ traders have sailed the waters of the $indian_ocean_region$ for generations, traveling impossibly far in search of rare and valuable goods. From the eastern coasts of $africa$, to the shores of $india$, and even as far as the spice islands of $indonesia_region$, the waters are crossed by vessels of the $muslim_ADJ$ faithful.

name: $muslim_ADJ$ Trade Communities
description: The presence of $muslim_ADJ$ traders in faraway lands puts them in contact with many different peoples and beliefs. The establishment of trade communities among them allows for a certain degree of blending and syncretism of their beliefs with the true Word of $muslim_god_name$.

name: Expansionist Faith
description: From its origins in $arabia_region$, $muslim$ has expanded far and fast. In a few generations, its believers spanned from $iberia_region$ to $india$, the most rapid religious expansion the world has ever seen. There are new lands waiting to be touched by our light, however — perhaps it is time for a second $muslim_ADJ$ expansion.

name: Blend of Influences
description: $muslim$ has expanded to many new places since its origins in $arabia_region$, and with this spread, it came into contact with many different peoples and ways of life. Many exchanges of influence happened during this process, to the point that many characteristics not originally part of $muslim$ have become intrinsically associated with the faith.

name: Islamic Schools
description: $muslim$ has always encouraged study and analysis of its scriptures, to the point where we have developed entirely different schools of thought on how to interpret them. Our scholars are therefore extremely learned in the $common_string_quran$ and our other holy texts, capable of having the most in-depth theological discussions.

name: Gunpowder Empires
description: Gunpowder may have been invented in the Far East, but it was through $muslim$ that it became widely used throughout the world. Gunpowder weapons have been a staple of our armies for generations, and its production and use is one of our defining characteristics.

name: Established Holy Sites
description: While other religions have somewhat lax and inconsistent views towards how their holy sites are used, the rules of $muslim$ about sacred places are quite clear. Our people will undoubtedly make their pilgrimages with the appropriate reverence and dignity.

name: Islamic Courts
description: The royal courts of $muslim_ADJ$ countries have always been among the most admired in the world. Praised for our refined culture and luxurious appointments, tales of the magnificence of our courts have spread far and wide, and our people take great pride in this reputation.

name: Schools of Thought
description: $muslim$ tradition has always emphasized the pursuit of knowledge and education. From schools of jurisprudence and theology to the great libraries and institutions of learning established by various rulers, $muslim_ADJ$ scholarship has earned admiration throughout the $muslim_ADJ$ world and well beyond.

name: Distant Trade Ventures
description: It is from the most distant places that the most lucrative trade goods come. For many years, $muslim_ADJ$ traders have traveled huge distances both on land and across the seas in search of profitable trade opportunities.

name: Resilient Traders
description: $muslim_ADJ$ traders endure the harshest of conditions during their expeditions. From crossing the scorching sands of the Sahara and Gobi Deserts, to braving the monsoon-plagued waters of the $indian_ocean_region$, they have proved time and again that they will undergo any hardship in order to bring about successful trade.

name: Jewels of the Desert
description: $muslim$ arose from the sands of $arabia_region$ and spread across a largely arid region. Yet some $muslim_ADJ$ cities became like prosperous jewels shining in the harsh desert, literal and figurative oasis made bountiful through trade, architecture, and irrigation. With wise investment and planning, any desert settlement can achieve a similar status.

name: Comprehensive Land Survey
description: In order to know who should pay taxes, we must first know who owns what. A comprehensive land survey, and regularly updating it, are therefore essential. We will always get what we are due!

name: Counting the People
description: Now that we know who owns what, the logical follow-up is to get a clearer idea of who lives where. This will tell us where to look when we need fresh recruits for our armies.

name: Cosmopolitan Court
description: People from all over admire the beauty and sophistication of our $muslim_ADJ$ court. We have therefore become an appealing destination for talented luminaries of all kinds, which only adds to our overall court vibrancy and prestige.

name: Ḵilāfa
description: The #italic Ḵilāfa#!, or Caliphate, is the union of all $muslim_ADJ$ faithful under a single ruler in the form of the $rank_empire_muslim_ruler_male$, who is to be the political and spiritual successor of Muḥammad, peace be upon him. Although there are different ideas about who is eligible to be $rank_empire_muslim_ruler_male$, the idea of all $muslim$ united under a single banner has always been the primary focus of this process.

name: $ibadi_ADJ$ Imamate
description: Unlike the $caliphate$ or a divinely appointed $shia_ADJ$ Imām, an $ibadi_ADJ$ Imām does not rule over the entirety of the $muslim_ADJ$ world, but instead governs locally. Every community can be ruled independently by its own Imām.

name: Contacts Network
description: The extensive reach of $muslim$ has brought $muslim_ADJ$ countries in contact with many different foreign lands. Maintaining a rich network of international contacts such as ours is always beneficial for diplomacy.

name: Infiltration Tactics
description: Although the ancient $nizari_school$ $shia_ADJ$ order of the #italic Ḥashshāshīyīn#! has been largely mythicized beyond their original scope, their tactics of subterfuge and assassination were undeniably effective. If we employ such infiltration tactics ourselves, we should benefit from the same success.

name: Unified Armies
description: It cannot be denied that $muslim$ has spread to many different cultures and peoples since its emergence in $arabia_region$. As long as they believe in $muslim_god_name$, any person should be able to fight in His name, regardless of their origin.

name: Harsh Environments
description: $muslim$ has, since its inception, found its way to civilizations in some of the harshest environments of the world. If anyone from outside our region tries to invade our territories, they will find it fiendishly difficult — as they should!

name: The Pentarchy
description: The old structure of the Church formulated by Emperor Justinian is still in full effect in $orthodox$. Although the patriarch of $rome$ believes himself to be above all else, for the #italic authentic#! Church, the cities of $constantinople$, $alexandria$, $antioch$, and $jerusalem$ remain far more important.

name: Imperial Creed
description: $orthodox$ has been the official faith of the Roman Empire ever since its adoption of $christian$. The heresies of the West and their falsely proclaimed 'emperors' will not be able to discredit our legitimacy.

name: Filioque Issue
description: The heretical addition of the #italic Filioque#! clause, which states that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father 'and the Son', was done without calling the appropriate ecumenical council, and therefore it is illegitimate. We are the guardians of the true prayer, and $rome$ shall be damned for their heresy!

name: Septuagint
description: Our Old Testament is encoded in $greek_language$, using the version known as the $septuagint$, which is a translation from $hebrew_language$ done in the 3rd century BC. It was written by seventy-two isolated translators, who all came up with the exact same translations independently. It is thus definitely divinely inspired, and the direct word of God.

name: Anagignoskomena
description: Our Bible contains all books worthy of veneration and study, even though some may have less importance than others. The $anagignoskomena$ are not present in the $hebrew_language$ Bible, so they receive less attention than other texts, but they are nonetheless worthy of being read and should not be disregarded.

name: Religious Icons
description: Icons are the physical representation of our faith, sacred depictions of holy figures designed to inspire awe and devotion to those that contemplate them.

name: Church Guidance
description: The Scriptures are the Word of God, but only the Church is able to interpret their correct meaning and to relate it accurately to the flock. Any independent reading or interpretation of the Scriptures outside of Church guidance would only lead to being lost in falsehoods and on the path to heresy.

name: Unchanging Tradition
description: The tradition passed down to us by Jesus Christ and the apostles is consistent, without any changes, additions, or subtractions whatsoever. Our faith is undeniable in its truths, and what is fundamentally true about this world cannot be changed by mortal hands.

name: Church Councils
description: As the Church must be united in its judgments, any matter too complex for a single bishop to resolve requires us to call a council, where the bishops will consult the mind of the Church itself. The council's decisions shall therefore reflect the consensus of the Church as a whole.

name: $greek_culture$ Rite
description: Our rites and canonical practices have been for centuries well-defined following the $greek_culture$ rites of $constantinople$. Although there may be some small variations in certain places, there is remarkable homogeneity in the rites performed throughout $orthodox$.

name: Physical Body of Christ
description: Our Church is the physical manifestation of the Body of Christ on Earth, having no difference from the one in Heaven. As such, the Church is the physical embodiment of the Lord Savior, sent for the benefit of His people.

name: Icon Veneration
description: The most important aspect of veneration is the faithful be reminded of great works, miracles, and figures through their natural sense. As such, our churches are adorned with vibrant images and colors, ringing with music and sweetly scented with our holy incense, so that the presence of Christ on Earth can be immediately felt by all inside.

name: Theotokos
description: The Virgin Mary is a key figure in our beliefs, as she fulfilled the Old Covenant by carrying within her the New Covenant in the figure of Christ. As such, being the bearer of Christ God-incarnate, she was literally the Mother of God, and has a place of prominence above all other saints.

name: Heavenly Architecture
description: $orthodox_ADJ$ religious buildings are designed in imitation of heaven. Their construction centralized around the basilica, the central dome that serves as a roof and symbolizes the heavens. Richly decorated in beautiful images and gleaming golden icons, they are a wonder to behold.

name: Iconostasis
description: One key feature of any $orthodox_ADJ$ church is that of the $iconostasis$, a wall of icons that separates the main body of the building from the altar. The icons it contains serve as a visualization of the link between the worshipers and the Holy of Holies, and thus the link between Heaven and the people, serving as a guide for the people towards Heaven.

name: Julian Calendar
description: The time of our country and our Church has been for centuries measured by the $julian_calendar$, promulgated by Julius Caesar in 46 BC. It not only unifies all eastern $christian_ADJ$ nations, but it also serves to dictate when the important feasts and celebrations are to be held.

name: Paschal Cycle
description: $orthodox$ contains some movable feasts around #italic Pascha#!, Easter, organized in the $paschal_cycle$. The ten weeks before Pascha are called #italic Triodion#!, while the fifty days after Pascha are called #italic Pentekostárion#!. This cycle marks the most important celebrations in the liturgical year.

name: Oktōēchos
description: An eight-mode system of writing music, the $oktoechos$ has been the system used for writing religious chants and music for the Church for centuries. It is the foundation of $orthodox_ADJ$ chant, although with some variations between cultures.

name: Prestigious Monasticism
description: In $orthodox$, monasticism and asceticism are highly valued and almost a requirement. Any bishop must be a monk first, and they must become a monk before being consecrated if they are not. As such, monasteries and monasticism centers have a big impact on our clerical life.

name: National Rites
description: The presence of different autocephalous patriarchates in our Church allows for certain variations between the national rites of each country. However, the unity of the message remains, and the Church as a single entity is not broken.

name: Heirs of Rome
description: Many have claimed to be the heirs of Rome and indeed the whole Roman Empire. However, only our religion is the true faith of the old Empire, and therefore only we can legitimately claim to be a direct descendant from it.

name: Legacy of Saint Andrew
description: According to legend, Saint Andrew himself visited Scythia and the northern shores of the $black_sea_area$, prophesying a great flourishing of $christian$ once he reached the future site of $kyiv$.

name: Christianization of the Slavs
description: The people of the Kievan Rus' were among the first of the Eastern $slavic_group$ people to accept the light of Christ and convert to $orthodox$. From there, the faith spread throughout the region.

name: Cyril and Methodius
description: Two $BYZ_ADJ$ theologians from the 9th century, these men were instrumental to the evangelization of the Slavs. They are credited for developing the Glagolitic alphabet, the first one to ever be used to transcribe $church_slavonic_language$, and their followers later developed the Cyrillic alphabet, naming it after Cyril in his honor.

name: Interaction Between Church and State
description: The patriarchates have absolute authority over their own jurisdictions and those who occupy them. By tying their authority to that of the ruler, we can take advantage of the resources of the Church, and use them to strengthen state authority.

name: Outwards Expansion
description: It is the holy duty of the Church to bring the light of Christ to the pagan and the infidels. We must go beyond our borders to carry salvation to every lost soul!

name: Justified Holy Wars
description: We cannot allow heathens and heretics to dictate our actions. It is our holy duty to cleanse the land of their impurity so that the true realm of God can be manifested on Earth.

name: Resistance to the Infidels
description: Our $orthodox_ADJ$ brethren have seen themselves at times under the yoke of foreign infidels. However, we have learned to endure such oppression, and even live in peace alongside these infidels.

name: Eastern Ecumenism
description: $christian_ADJ$ denominations from the Oriental Orthodoxy are often confused with Eastern $orthodox$ by the uninitiated. Although they are different from us in many key issues, they are still $christian_ADJ$, and our many commonalities could be used to bring them back to the correct faith.

name: Structured Patriarchates
description: Our patriarchates have always been well organized and structured, each with its own attributions and delimitations. This allows for a better-functioning Church, which leads to a better-functioning state.

name: Welcome the Unwelcome
description: While we have seen the light of the true faith, many of our brethren suffer under the oppressive rule of misguided heathens. We should invite these people to settle in our lands, where they can process their faith without repercussions and, more importantly, contribute to our treasury.

name: Efficient Tax Collectors
description: Previously, the clerics shouldered a significant portion of the tax burden. While some of these structures have been dismantled in the wake of the Reformation, the capable common people are still around, and thus must help make up for that missing clerical revenue.

name: A New Confession
description: The Reformation gives us the opportunity to define a new creed for our people and, more importantly, to accept critique and make adjustments accordingly.

name: Devotionalism
description: We must revive Augustinian theology, and recognize that our beliefs are built on the emotions and fervor of the faithful.

name: Shield of the Faith
description: Our religion is beset on all sides by enemies. We will have to defend our rights to our own confession against the $catholic_ADJ$ oppressors.

name: Expulsion of Heretics
description: The troublesome heretics in our domain could easily foment rebellion against our ruler. It would be better if we redirected them to our overseas colonies instead, where they can cause less trouble.

name: Repurposed Monasteries
description: Former religious properties seized by the state during our national conversion process can serve us now in new ways, such as centers for production or administration.

name: Involved Laity
description: With the increased involvement of the laity in the day-to-day administration of our Church, our people have found a more personal connection to the faith itself.

name: $catholic_cuius_regio_eius_religio$
description: $catholic_cuius_regio_eius_religio_desc$

name: Protestant Art
description: The Reformation has given our artists the opportunity to explore new themes, finally freed from the obligatory glorification of God. Hiring more of these artists will reflect well on us, and give us the reputation of being a great patron of the arts.

name: $sunday_schools_advance$
description: $sunday_schools_advance_desc$

name: Diligent Workers
description: The influence of Puritan and Pietist preachers on the Reformation is undeniable. Their emphasis on virtues like diligence and frugality will help us to foster an industrious and dedicated workforce.

name: Embrace Romanticism
description: In the wake of the Enlightenment's emphasis on reason, we must not forget the power of emotion and imagination. By embracing Romanticism, which celebrates nature, folklore, and national character, our artists will produce works that stir the soul.

name: Defense Against Heretics
description: We will need to be wary of forces trying to convert our people, or seduce them back to our previous faith. By publicly declaring these preachers to be malicious and hostile, we can prepare our people for these interactions and more easily reinforce religious orthodoxy.

name: Protestant Innovations
description: Since the founding days of our faith, we have emphasized the inherent value of questioning established doctrines and beliefs. We should apply these same ethics to other fields of study.

name: Heian-Kyō
description: The city of Heian-Kyō has been the residence of the Emperor for centuries, and is a center for art and culture. It is there where the lavish court of the $fujiwara_dynasty$ flourished, and all the people in $JAP$ looked to it with awe and inspiration. We shall embrace its traditional role, and with our patronage make the culture of our capital flourish once again.

name: Matsuri
description: Every local shrine and temple has its own festivals and celebrations. The people are always eager to participate, for it is their chance to offer devotion and gratitude towards their local protector #italic Kami#!.

name: Onmyōdō
description: Coming from $china$ centuries ago, the theories of Yīn and Yáng evolved in $JAP$ into $onmyodo$. Expert practitioners, called #italic onmyōji#!, deal with the purification and exorcism of evil and vengeful spirits, as well as with divination, astronomy, and the study of nature.

name: Sumō
description: Derived from an ancient agricultural ritual, in which dances served as prayers for a good harvest, the practice of $sumo$ has escaped the confines of the court and is now a popular practice among the commoners. It also serves as a form of combat training.

name: Nanto Rokushū
description: The temples of $nara$ have been influential since $buddhist$ first came from $china$. The six schools that formed around these temples are a renowned repository of knowledge, especially about the teachings of the Buddha and the various ways of achieving enlightenment. However, they also teach more mundane, but equally valuable subjects, such as how to properly administrate a monastery.

name: Shinbutsu-Shūgō
description: Since $buddhist$ came to $japan_region$, its teachings have coexisted with the worship of local #italic Kami#!. This has led to them both blending into a single combined set of beliefs, albeit with distinct ritualistic practices.

name: Honji Suijaku
description: One of the key practices in $shinbutsu_shuugou$ is to identify the local #italic Kami#! as manifestations of the different Buddha, and the Buddhas as manifestations of the different #italic Kami#!. In the end, they are one and the same, with core forms or #italic Honji#! taking on different aspects, or #italic suijaku#!.

name: Hachiman Worship
description: Hachiman is one of the most venerated divinities. Originally a deification of Ōjin Tennō, after the introduction of $buddhist$ he was later also identified as a Bodhisattva. He is the protector of the Imperial line and the tutelary god of the warrior class.

name: Gozan Jissetsu
description: The 'Five Mountains System' originated in $china$ from state-sponsored Chán $buddhist_ADJ$ monasteries, atop the holy mountains that gave the system its name. In $japan_region$, the practice continued in the $kamakura$ period by the sponsoring of the Zen temples, the Five Mountains of $kyoto$ and the Five Mountains of $kamakura$. By maintaining our sponsorship of such institutions, we can use them to help stabilize our rule.

name: Bodaiji
description: Since antiquity, our people have venerated our ancestors. The most influential of our rulers erect entire temples, where they will be entombed and then worshiped after death, and where their deeds and words will be remembered for all time.

name: Kagura
description: Originally sacred ritual dances performed in front of the court by the #italic miko#!, the shrine maidens, the $kagura$ also inspired the performance of popular ritual dances all around $japan_region$. These dances have evolved into a myriad of forms, but all of them preserving the tradition and ritual they come from.

name: Obon
description: One of the most important festivals in our culture, $obon$ is the time to honor the dead, and our ancestors in particular. During the celebrations, offerings of food and ritual dances are performed. People also light fires and lanterns to guide the souls of the dead back home for the celebrations, and once again back to the land of the dead.

name: Neo-$SECT_CONFUCIANISM_NAME$
description: $SECT_CONFUCIANISM_NAME$ has a millenary history, and Neo-$SECT_CONFUCIANISM_NAME$ has already existed in $japan_region$ for centuries. However, active state involvement and support of the faith will strengthen our authority.

name: Danka System
description: For centuries, households in $japan_region$ have had close relationships with local $buddhist_ADJ$ temples, giving them financial patronage in exchange for the temples taking care of their spiritual needs. Formally enforcing this system will keep our people devoted to the faith, and secure the vital role our religion plays in society.

name: Harae
description: In our faith, the practice of #italic $harae$#!, or ritual purification, is key to removing all #italic tsumi#!, sins, and #italic kegare#!, spiritual uncleanness. Mandating that our population performs the $harae$ rituals properly and frequently ensures that our country remains spiritually pure.

name: Jisha-Bugyō
description: The administrator and supervisor of all the temples and shrines, the $jisha_bugyou$ also oversees the activities these religious institutions perform, making sure that their interests align with those of the government.

name: Kokugaku
description: Almost since its inception as a country, $japan_region$ and $shinto$ have been influenced by foreign ideas coming from $china$ and $buddhist$. A new movement is taking root, claiming that our own national spirit is naturally pure, and that our society must be cleansed of any foreign influences.

name: Home Shrines
description: Ritual and religious practice have been traditionally relegated to shrines and temples. However, more and more of our people are placing in their homes both local family shrines, called #italic kamidana#!, to venerate the Kami, and #italic butsudan#! as $buddhist_ADJ$ altars for their ancestors.

name: Fukko $shinto$
description: As people are rejecting foreign influence in our culture, they are also starting to reject the teachings of $buddhist_ADJ$ and $SECT_CONFUCIANISM_NAME$ interfering in our faith. Given this emerging demand for doctrinal purity, a formal revitalization of $shinto$ might be wise.
